articleTitle: Broadband Dual Polarization Antenna Array for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband dual-polarization antenna array operating at millimeter wave band (24-29 GHz) for 5G cellular communication is presented. The antenna unit achieves dual-polarized and unidirectional broadside radiation. The proposed antenna also possesses a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 22.2% and a port isolation of more than 14.7dB. This work further extends to a 1×4 array antenna with an isolation better than 14.3 dB. Under the premise of the edge angle gain decreases less than 3 dB, the beam-scanning array can realize a scanning angle from - 57.71 degrees to +73.75 degrees with the peak gain of 10.45 dBi and a scanning angle from -66.51 degrees to +62.61 degrees with the peak gain of 9.73 dBi when the port 1-1~ port 1-4 and port 2-1~ port 2-4 are excited respectively at 27GHz.

articleTitle: A Transparent Dual-Band Dual-Polarized mm-Wave Antenna Array for 5G Smartphone Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A transparent dual-band dual-polarized mm-wave antenna array working at 28 GHz and 39 GHz for the fifth generation mobile communications (5G) is proposed to enable the integrated design with the mobile phone rear glass. The antenna array configuration consists of radiating stacked patch integrated into the mobile phone real glass and feed section in the low-loss flexible PCB as a solution to save enormous PCB area. Radiation performance of the 1×4 antenna array integrated on the rear glass of smartphone is analyzed and indium tin oxide is employed as the transparent conducting oxide. Based on the simulation results, the 10 dB return loss of the antenna array ranges from 24 to 30 GHz and from 36 to 40.5 GHz to cover the major released 5G mm-Wave bands of n257, n258, n261 and n260 in the third generation partnership project (3GPP). The integrated antenna array can provide a high array gain in both operating bands, making it suitable for 5G smartphone applications.

articleTitle: Terahertz Broadband Self-Compensating Waveguide Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband self-compensating waveguide phase shifter which is easy to be realized in terahertz band is proposed in this paper. The phase shifts generated by widened waveguide and periodic grooves both vary with frequency, while following opposite trend. By properly combining these two different phase shifting structures, the bandwidth of the proposed phase shifter is significantly improved. A terahertz self-compensating 90° waveguide phase shifter is designed and simulated, taking account of the nonideal boundary conditions caused by the manufacturing process. The results of the proposed phase shifter show that in the frequency band from 275 to 385 GHz, the phase deviation is less than 3°, and the insertion loss is better than -0.2dB. The performances reveal its application potential in terahertz broadband feeding network.

articleTitle: A Design of Decoupling Structure MIMO Antenna for Mutual Coupling Reduction in 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new antenna structure with low mutual coupling between 2 antenna elements for MIMO has been developed and presented in this paper. The decoupling structure has been analyzed and designed between both antennas to suppress the isolation between dual elements. Nine different structures has been designed and 28.75% improvement on isolation has been achieved from pattern 3 decoupling structure. By using the decoupling structure, the antenna bandwidth has been improved tremendously to 20.8%. The antenna has been printed with full copper ground on the bottom layer. The antenna was simulated and optimized at 16 GHz using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) with permittivity, r = 2.2 and thickness, h = 1.57mm on Rodges RT-Duroid 5885 substrate. The antennas are matched at their corresponding frequency of operations. The simulation and fabrication results have shown that the antenna works well.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Reconfigurable Transmitarrray Element Using a Novel Phase Shifter with Varactors and PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel wideband electronically reconfigurable transmitarray antenna element with continuous transmission phase tuning at 5.8 GHz. The element is based on a multi-layer receiver-transmitter structure. A 180° analog phase shifter loaded with varactors and a 0° / 180° 1-bit phase shifter loaded with two PIN-diodes are combined to provide 360° electronic phase tuning capability. Full wave simulations show that the transmission magnitude loss is between 0.85 dB and 1.25 dB at 5.8 GHz when the transmission phase changes. A wideband 3-dB transmission bandwidth of 17% is also achieved.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Wideband Dual-Polarized 5G mm-Wave Antenna-in-Package (AiP) Array for Cellular Phones
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design of a miniaturized wideband dual-polarized linear antenna-in-package (AiP) array consisting of 4 antenna elements is proposed for cellular phones with fifth generation mobile communications (5G) mm-Wave technologies. Based on |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nn</sub>| ≤ -10 dB, both of the two polarization (pol.) of the AiP array can cover from 24.99 GHz to 30.10 GHz and from 36.18 GHz to 40.26 GHz. The third generation partnership project (3GPP) bands n257, n261, and n260 can hence be accommodated as the local main bands. For band n258, the worst | S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nn</sub> | values for both the two pol. are -7.52 dB, which are better than -6.0 dB. Band n258 can thus be covered as the roaming band. Scanning peak realized gains for both the two pol. are 9.57 dBi, 10.30 dBi, and 11.99 dBi at 26.0 GHz, 28.0 GHz, and 39.0 GHz, respectively. The whole size of the AiP array is 1.616 mm × 4.84 mm × 18.60 mm, i.e., 0.13 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 0.39 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 1.50 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> at 24.25 GHz.

articleTitle: Elevation Angle Characteristics of Clutter Loss in Urban Areas for Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a clutter-loss generation model that considers elevation angle characteristics to help advance the examination of clutter loss to promote common use between satellite or aerial communications and terrestrial mobile communications such as cellular systems. In this paper, we derive the elevation angle characteristics of clutter loss using conventional estimate formulas for propagation loss. We show that clutter loss is inversely proportional to the square of the elevation angle. We compare the examination results to those for ITU-R P.2108, and present the differences. The multiple screen diffraction model is known as a theoretical model for propagation loss in cellular environment. This model is applied in a macro cell environment. The proposal model is applied to the microcell environment which is the mainstream currently.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Slot Coupling Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel 12 × 12 digital reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) antenna is designed using an aperture-coupled microstrip patch structure to realize high gain beam scanning. With the PIN diode ON and OFF, Phase difference within 180° ± 20° of each reflectarray element is realized from 8.4 to 9.2 GHz. Utilizing this 1-bit element, the 12 × 12 reconfigurable reflectarray antenna is designed. Then designing a DC control board independently adjusts all diodes. The simulation results show that beam scanning within ±40° can be achieved both from 8 to 9.2 GHz, which means optimizing the initial phase distribution of the aperture surface can improve the beam-scanning and gain performance.

articleTitle: Inline Asymmetric Response Quarter-mode SIW Bandpass Filters with Controllable Mixed Electric and Magnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports a novel mixed electric and magnetic coupling (MEMC) structure, which is constructed by two coupled quarter-mode substrate-integrated waveguide (QMSIW) cavities with an interdigital coupling structure and a direct-connected metal strip. The proposed MEMC is analyzed in detail, and it has the merits of compact size and controllable MEMC. Using one MEMC between two QMSIW cavities, one controllable finite transmission zero (FTZ) can be produced at almost any location. For the demonstration, two inline fourth-order QMSIW bandpass filters (BPFs) with one lower FTZ and one upper FTZ, respectively, were designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results agree well with simulated ones.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Broadband Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna with High Gain and its Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized and high-gain antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) is presented in the paper. Plasmonic metamaterials are loaded to the edges of the antenna for miniaturization and high gain. The antenna with size of 94×70×1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> was simulated by use of CST. The simulated impedance band is from 1.8 GHz to more than 10 GHz. Meanwhile, the gain of the antenna can be increased by 2 dB in the range from 2 GHz to 6 GHz. A 1x8 Vivaldi phased array is presented. Its scanning angle is over ±45° and the gain can reach 15 dBi at 4 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Reflective Metasurface Based on Cross-Shaped Resonator for 5G Wireless Communication Systems at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a dual-polarized reflective metasurface for 5G wireless communication systems at 28 GHz is presented. The metasurface configuration is composed of an array of cross-shaped resonators of different sizes that are regarding to an organization of reflection phase based on energy surface channeling technique. By properly designing the metasurface on a surface area of 15λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×15λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, it can anomalously reflect both TE- and TM-polarized incident plane waves from θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> = 0° to θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 70°, while achieving a radiation power ratio of the main reflected beam to its sidelobe of over 10 dB.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain Circularly Polarized Antenna Array on Gap Waveguide for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) antenna array based on gap waveguide (GW) is presented in this paper. Firstly, a CP antenna based on septum polarizer is designed as the element for the array. Secondly, the feeding network is composed of T-junctions and realized by ridge gap waveguide (RGW). Then a 16 × 16 antenna array is built up by the elements. The novelty of this antenna is the combination of planar array and septum polarizer based on GW technology to achieve circularly polarization, high gain and high efficiency in wide bandwidth. The proposed array antenna achieves wide impedance bandwidth of 34.5% with the reflection coefficient below -10 dB, and a wide 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 26.5%. The simulated gain is higher than 32 dBic from 24.5 to 32.0 GHz, and the antenna efficiency is larger than 90%.

articleTitle: A ±45° Dual-Polarized Antenna for 5G mmWave Applications Based on Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A ±45° dual-polarized antenna is designed based on the gap waveguide technology which offers a low loss and easy-to-manufacture solution at the mmWave frequencies. Dual-polarized antennas help to increase the capacity and coverage of a wireless system and also decrease the overall cost. Two parallel arrays of 8 slots each are employed to create the orthogonal polarizations. The antenna operates in the 24.25 - 27.25 GHz frequency band. The simulated average gain of each polarization is 14.5 dBi while achieving a cross-polarization isolation of at least 15 dB.

articleTitle: A Compact Antenna Based on Metasurface for WLAN Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a compact antenna based on metasurface. The working frequency of the proposed antenna covers the industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) 2.45 GHz band. The metasurface of this design, consists of a 3×3 array of the unit cells. A printed coplanar waveguide (CPW) monopole antenna is used to feed the metasurface. Unlike the traditional antennas based metasurface that the metasurface as a reflector, the metasurface of this design acts as a radiator and works in the operating frequency band, which can significantly decrease the dimension of the antenna. The size of the antenna is 0. 094 $\lambda _0^2$, and the wideband of 11.02 % is achieved with S11 below -10 dB. The total efficiency is over 88% and the maximum gain is 3.3 dBi in the operating frequency band. This design is a promising candidate in wireless communication.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Radio Tomographic Imaging Technique using Multipath Components for Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we propose a new radio tomographic imaging (RTI) technique, called Multipath-RTI, using millimeter-wave (mm-wave) radios such as 5G mobile and WiGig LAN systems, which will realize a highly accurate device-free human movement monitoring for smart home/smart building applications. Utilizing the features that mm-wave radios usually have high delay and angle resolution, and thus is capable of separating the multi-path components (MPCs), the Multipath-RTI can drastically reduce the number of sensor nodes by using the virtual nodes created by multipaths. This article presented the fundamental operation verification by ray-tracing simulations, and also showed the feasibility study by mm-wave propagation measurements.

articleTitle: Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna With Seven Switchable Beams in Elevation Plane
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a pattern-reconfigurable antenna is proposed that provides multiple switchable beams. By reconfiguring parasitic striplines placed around a radiating dipole and reflector under the dipole using p-i-n diodes, the antenna main beam can be switched to seven directions in the elevation plane, which are 0,30,55,120. The proposed antenna operates from 2.4Ghz to 2.5Ghz with dimensions of about 0.69λ×0.69 λ×0.69 λ. The prototype of the antenna was simulated and optimized in HFSS. For all directional beams, the simulated S11 values are below -10dB, and the simulated realized gains range from 7.5 to 8.3dBi.

articleTitle: A dual-polarized miniaturized Vivaldi antenna with resistance loading
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized Vivaldi antenna is designed based on the traditional Vivaldi antenna using resistive loading technology. The antenna is in the form of a two-layer Vivaldi design with feeders between two dielectric plates that are fed using CPW. The length of the antenna is only 168mm*70mm*1mm. After being loaded with a resistor, the VSWR is less than 2 in the working frequency (0.4~6GHz) .

articleTitle: Stage identification using electromagnetic waves for noncontact bed sores detection system
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Bed sores are injuries caused by pressures on the skin for a long time and obstructions of blood flows. As the injury progresses, the treatment period becomes longer. In addition, surgery is required in some cases. Therefore, early detection is important. In this report, we are engaged in developing the noncontact bed sores detection system by using electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of Helix-Loaded, High Gain Planar Endfire Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Conceptual design of a helix-loaded, high gain planar endfire circularly polarized antenna (PECPA) is envisioned. An axial-mode helix is excited by a complementary dipole PECPA at its basic form, while a low profile of about 0.034-wavelength is maintained. In this way, endfire directivity and front-to-back ratio (FTBR) can be enhanced to 7.1dBi and 14dB, respectively. Design considerations with preliminary numerical results on key parameters of the proposed antenna are discussed.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Wideband Circularly Polarized Reflectarray with Linearly Polarized Feed
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer wideband circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray with linearly polarized (LP) feed is presented. First, a wideband multi-resonance dual-LP unit cell consisting of five split rhombus rings is proposed. The element has high isolations between two polarizations and preferable linear phase responses in wide frequency band. Then, according to the reflectarray phase distributions to calculate the dimensions of each element. Finally, a 15x15 CP reflectarray antenna is simulated by ANYSY HFSS. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna can achieve 31.4% 3-dB gain bandwidth (11.6-16 GHz) and 35% 3-dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth (11.1-16 GHz) Its peak gain is 25.9 dBi at 13.8 GHz.

articleTitle: DRA-Fed Broadband Metasurface Antennas Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A metasurface antenna fed by rectangular dielectric resonator antenna is proposed for broadband application with reduced backward radiation. The feasibility of proposed feeding structure is verified by using characteristic mode analysis. A dominate mode of metasurface and the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ11</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup> mode of DRA both with a broadside radiation pattern are simultaneously excited to widen impedance bandwidth. The simulation achieves a 29.7% impedance bandwidth of 4.67-6.30 GHz for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<; -10 dB and a boresight gain of 6-9 dBi over the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Indoor Line-of-Sight Probability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a computational machine learning based approach for line-of-sight (LOS) probability prediction in indoor environments. An artificial neural network (ANN) based model is finally employed to predict the LOS probability indoors. k-nearest neighbours (k-NN) and gradient boosted decision trees (GBDT) based models are trained as baselines against the ANN based model. The proposed model is validated by Monte Carlo simulations and compared with state-of-the-art LOS probability approaches. It is further employed in computing the coverage rate for a Poisson point process (PPP) distributed indoor small cell network, which is also validated through comparison with Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: A Broadband Single-Layer Reflectarray Antenna Based on Tightly Coupled Dipole
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel broadband single-layer reflectarray antenna based on tightly coupled dipole is proposed in this paper. Each element consists of a tightly coupled dipole and a slot line. The phase compensation is realized by adjusting the length of the slot lines. Due to the strong coupling among neighboring elements, the unit cell is able to provide a linear phase response with sufficient phase variation range over a wide frequency range. Based on the proposed element, a reflectarray with 210 elements operating at 12-22 GHz is designed. The element distance is 3.2 mm, which is approximately 0.13λ of the lowest operating frequency. Within the designed frequency band, the radiation pattern of the reflectarray antenna is stable and the shape of main beam is not distorted or split. The simulated results show that the maximum gain at 21.5 GHz is about 21.3 dB and the maximum aperture efficiency at 21 GHz is about 46%. The cross-pol levels of the reflectarray are below -32 and -20 dB in the E- and H- planes, respectively.

articleTitle: Impact of Foliage on Urban MmWave Wireless Propagation Channel: A Ray-tracing Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The foliage has a significant impact on wireless communications under the millimeter wave band. Ray-tracing is a widely used technique to build an accurate wireless channel model. A drawback of ray-tracing is its high complexity. Therefore, using the ray-tracing method to build channel model with complex scatterers like trees results in a high computational burden. In this paper, we propose a hybrid ray-tracing based channel model for wireless channel simulation under typical urban scenario. In the proposed hybrid channel model, the correlation-based channel model is employed to model complex scatterers, e.g., trees, to reduce the computational complexity. Numerical results show that the hybrid model can capture the foliage influence on the wireless channel at the millimeter wave band well.

articleTitle: Multi-Frequency Millimeter-Wave Large-Scale Path Loss Characterization for Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) band provides abundant spectrum to meet the anticipated demands of system capacity in the fifth generation (5G) wireless networks. This paper presents a measurement-based analysis of large-scale propagation characteristics in conference room across four 5G mmWave candidate bands (i.e., 25.5, 28, 37.5, and 39.5 GHz). Using the flexible mmWave channel sounder, the effect of receiver locations (e.g., on the ground and desktop) is investigated with a focus on path loss, shadow fading, and cross-polarization ratio (XPR). Omnidirectional channel sounding data using the same measurement configurations reveals that path loss exponents in general increase with increasing carrier frequency for copolarization channels, while XPRs probably seen to be frequency- independent at 25.5-39.5 GHz band.

articleTitle: A Multiband Cross- and Circular Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a single layered anisotropic high efficient multiband cross- and circular polarizer is modeled and analyzed. The unit cell of the proposed anisotropic metasurface contains a curved double-head anchors. The metasurface gives linear to linear polarization conversion (cross-polarization) with in frequency ranges of 5.8-6.15, 10.2-16.15 and 19.65-19.92 GHz with more than 90% efficiency. Moreover, linear to circular polarization conversion is achieved over three frequency bands of 5.50-5.56, 6.62-8.93 and 16.2-18.92 GHz. The response of the metasurface is stable up to 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>.The proposed metasurface has numerous applications in polarization control devices.

articleTitle: A Compact Frequency Reconfigurable Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of compact frequency reconfigurable antenna by loading four pin diodes. The antenna is constructed of a rectangular patch and two curved parasitic patches. Four PIN diodes are inserted between the rectangular patch located in the center and two curved parasitic patches along the long sides of the rectangular patch. By altering the states of the PIN diodes, the proposed antenna can operate at 2.71 GHz, 4.73 GHz, 5.35 GHz and 6.16 GHz. The antenna maintains stable radiation pattern in all operating modes. These advantages make it a promising candidate for WIFI/WIMAX and future wireless communication systems. The designed structure has a compact dimension of 0.47 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with an extremely thin thickness of 0.01 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> represents to the lowest operating frequency.

articleTitle: Array Source Excitation Synthesis Using Approach of MIMO Maximum Power Transfer Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The maximum power transfer efficiency between multiple transmitting antennas and receiving antennas (MIMO) has been formulated by using eigenvalues of the matrix based on either Z matrix or S matrix [1]. The optimizable distribution of excitations for each element antenna of the transmitting array can be determined by an eigenvalue equation derived from the Rayleigh quotient for the power transmission efficiency. Now, in this paper, the method is applied to design the optimal excitations of transmitting array antenna to direct the maximum radiation to the desired direction. Moreover, the radiation patterns used different optimal excitations which correspond with the separation distance between the receiving and transmitting antenna are compared.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Circularly Polarized Planar Array Antenna Using Single-Arm-Spiral Elements and Dielectric-based IMGW
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultra-wideband circularly polarized (CP) planar array antenna is proposed in this paper. Using the concept of tightly coupled array antenna, the single-arm spiral element obtains good impedance matching and axial ratio (AR) characteristics in an ultra-wide frequency range. The new single-arm spiral element has a single-arm feeding structure which can be easily connected with the feeding network throughout a via. The feeding network is achieved by using dielectric-based inverted microstrip gap waveguide (IMGW) technology. An 8 × 8 CP planar array is designed. The simulated results show that the proposed array achieves a relative impedance bandwidth of 52.8% from 17.87 to 30.7 GHz and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 49.2% from 18.6 to 30.75 GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Pattern Reconfigurable Yagi-Uda Antenna Using Bistable Composite Laminates
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a pattern reconfigurable Yagi-Uda antenna based on bistable structural materials is designed. The antenna comprises a director, a driven dipole, a reflector and a substrate. By applying composite laminates as the substrate that holds two stable configurations with opposite curvations, the pattern reconfiguration performance can be realized, where the direction of maximum radiation differs between two states by 114°. This antenna operates at 2.4 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 10%, a gain of 7.49 dB and a front-to-back ratio of 8.2 dB. This design can be applied to aircraft control systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Automotive Millimeter Wave SAR in Curved Tracks
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Automatic operating system for vehicle has been widely studied. Especially, automotive millimeter-wave (MMW) radar has been attracting attentions. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) processing by using MMW radar can obtain high-resolution 2-D images. In general, SAR processing is used in straight orbits. However, in the case of automobiles, it is necessary to consider not only straight tracks but also curved tracks. In this paper, we show that the performance of automotive MMW-SAR processing on curved tracks by experimental results.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of 5G Millimeter-wave Phased Array Antenna for Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the bandwidth enhancement of the 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) phased array antenna. A reference millimeter-wave phased array antenna is designed first without the parasitic strips, copper frame and shorting vias, which works at 26.59 GHz operating frequency. The reference antenna has impedance bandwidth of 13.6%. For the case of proposed phased array antenna, parasitic strips, copper frame and shorting vias technique are integrated. Analysis shows that the parasitic strips, copper frame and shorting vias enhance the operational bandwidth of the proposed antenna with a good isolation performance as compared to the reference antenna. The impedance bandwidth of the reference mmWave antenna is 13.6 % GHz which got enhanced to 18.3 % at 25.72 GHz frequency of with parasitic strips. The impedance bandwidth is suitable for the 5G millimeter-wave phased array Mobile Communication applications.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Balanced Filtering Antenna with High Common-Mode Suppression
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A reconfigurable planar balanced quasi-Yagi antenna integrated with a bandpass filtering response is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a balanced stepped-impedance microstrip-slotline transition structure, a driver dipole, a pin diode, a parasitic strip and a bandpass filtering unit. A differential-mode (DM) assband with a sharp filtering performance is realized by introducing a microstrip stub-loaded resonator (SLR). By pin diode over the open-stub of SLR, the effective electrical length of the antenna can be changed, leading to an electrically tunable operating bandwidth. The antenna maintains radiation performance similar to that of the conventional quasi-Yagi antenna. Meanwhile, there are two radiation nulls on both sides of the passband to enhance the selectivity greatly. For the common-mode (CM) signals, the microstrip-slotline transition structure can achieve a good wideband CM suppression without affecting the DM ones, thus simplify the design procedure.

articleTitle: A Wideband High Directivity Dual-Polarized Millimeter-Wave Fabry-Perot Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband high directivity dual-polarized millimeter-wave Fabry-Perot resonator antenna is proposed in this letter. This design consists of dual-polarized antenna, a metal ground and partially reflective surface (PRS). This antenna can achieve wideband high directivity with the reflection phase of metamaterial versus frequency in a positive gradient. A 8×8 array of metamaterial elements is placed at the height of one-half of the working wavelength of the antenna. The optimization results show that the gain bandwidth of the millimeter wave resonator antenna can reach 17.9% and the peak gain is 14.7 dBi with good dual polarization performance.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency 90° Polarization Rotator Based on Split-Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on the regulation of the polarization state of electromagnetic(EM) wave by metamaterials, the application of polarization rotator in C-band is studied in this paper. Firstly, a double-layer 90° polarization rotator is proposed and analyzed. The top layer is a split-ring resonator, the bottom layer is a grating, and a Fabry-Perot(F-P) cavity is formed between them to enhance the polarization conversion efficiency. Results show the polarization is able to rotate vertical incident linearly polarized waves by 90° in the frequency range from 6.50 to 7.20 GHz. The cross-polarized transmission component can only reach 75%, so a three-layer 90° polarization rotator is proposed to improve it. The simulation results show that the frequency band from 6.47 to 7.21 GHz with a minimum of 98% cross-polarization transmission coefficient is achieved, co-polarization transmission coefficient is less than 5%, and the cross polarization transmission coefficient is up to 99.48% at the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized dual-polarized base station antenna is proposed. The antenna radiator consists of the conventional crossed loop dipoles. The radiator of the proposed antenna is miniaturized by loading an angular metal structure at the end of the dipole arm and an annular parasitic structure below the radiator. The size of the radiator is reduced from 52.5 × 52.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.39λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.39λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at 2.2GHz) to 41.5×41.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.3λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.3λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), so the edge length of the radiator is decreased by nearly 21%. Simulation results show that the antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 45% with S11 <; -15dB (1.7-2.7 GHz), and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub><; -25 dB. Within the operating bandwidth, the average gain is close to 8dBi and the half-power beamwidth is about 72±3°.

articleTitle: A tri-band notched Ultra-wideband MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, a compact ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with a high isolation covering 3.1-10.6 GHz UWB bands is presented. The proposed antenna is based on planar monopoles, and three band rejections are achieved by adding three Archimedes spiral electromagnetic band gap (As-EBG) structures. Isolation between two radiators is improved by suppressing the surface current flow through the T-shaped strip and triangular slot on the ground plane. The proposed antenna has a low mutual coupling of less than -20 dB over the target band (3.1-10.6 GHz). Therefore, the proposed antenna is a good candidate for UWB MIMO portable applications.

articleTitle: Far field estimation by current distribution reconstruction from hemispherical near field
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents current distribution reconstructing method for vehicular antennas using hemispherical near field. For electronically large antennas, far field measurements are very difficult and near field measurements are applied. The proposed method is an inverse problem using near field and enables the far field estimation with high accuracy by introducing Hermitian transpose, which is verified in simulations.

articleTitle: A Low Sidelobe Double-Layer Corporate-Feed Array Antenna by Inverted Microstrip Gap Waveguide at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a novel low sidelobe array antenna is designed at 28 GHz. The proposed array antenna is fed by classic full-corporate double-layer distribution networks based on newly introduced inverted microstrip gap waveguide. In order to achieve low sidelobe property, a classic Taylor synthesis method is adopted in this work. In the distribution network, a couple of unequal power dividers with identical output phases are applied for the low sibelobe in this work. The fundamental radiator is 2×2 slot sub-array, and the entire array antenna is constructed by 8×8 of such kind sub-arrays. The simulated radiation patterns show that the first sidelobe levels, front-back ratio of both E-plane and H-plane from 26.5 GHz to 29.5 GHz are very well improved compared with traditional ones with the equal amplitude and phase distribution networks. The input impedance bandwidth is about 12% with the reflection coefficient below -10 dB, and the gain is more than 29 dBi from 26.5 GHz to 29.5 GHz.

Author Keywords: low sidelobes and unequal power dividers with identical output phases

articleTitle: Analysis of Different Feeding Techniques on Textile Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wearable technology had brought inspiration to the development of textile antenna. However, the performance of a textile antenna is very sensitive and very unstable since there are many tolerance issues such as stretch effect, humidity effect and bending effect that shall be taken into account due to the flexible textile structure that may cause performance degradation. Thus, the crucial step to ensure that the antenna can perform well is to identify the most suitable feed line technique. The key for an antenna to work efficiently is to ensure maximum power transfer between the source and the antenna, such as the signal is fed at a point where the input impedance is 50 ohms. This paper presents the analysis of different feeding techniques applied on the proposed textile antenna. In this study, coaxial feed technique and transmission line feed technique are analyzed. The simulation is done in CST software and the antenna is fabricated to validate its performance. The investigation shows that the coaxial feed technique is more suitable to be used because the correct input impedance can be achieved easily in fabrication as compared to the transmission feed line technique and have more advantages as per discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Semi-Circular HMSIW Cavity Antenna Using Higher-Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band semi-circular half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) cavity antenna using higher-order modes is proposed. The HMSIW cavity is excited by the coplanar waveguide and microstrip feedline, leading to multiresonance. In order to improve the impedance bandwidth of the multiband, a semi-circular extended substrate loading the HMSIW cavity is integrated into a single substrate, and metallic vias of a circular distribution located in two semi-circular structures are designed to obtain dual band and high gain by suppressing the undesired interference modes. The prototype of the proposed antenna is manufactured and measured, demonstrating that a dual-band of 36.4-37.2 GHz and 44.2-45.4 GHz can be obtained with the peak gains of 10 dBi and 8.5 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Reflectionless Tapered Slotline Antenna with Resistive Absorption Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband reflectionless tapered slotline antenna with resistive absorption structure is proposed. The resistive absorption structure, composed of inductance and resistance, absorbs the low frequency components which cannot be radiated by the antenna. Meanwhile, the influence of absorption structure on the high frequency components is minimized, so that the high frequency components can flow into the Gaussian tapered slotline antenna as unaffected as possible. The return loss of the proposed reflectionless antenna is greater than 10 dB in most frequencies from DC-10 GHz, and the antenna has good endfire characteristics in the bandwidth of 2-10 GHz. Reflectionless antenna provides a realizable idea for expanding the bandwidth of UWB pulse antenna and can be employed in endfire application scenarios.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Leaky Wave Antennas Based on Oddmode Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an odd-mode spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP)-based dual-band leaky wave antenna is investigated. The feeding structure can equally split the energy into two parts and generate odd-mode signal. Odd-mode signal is excited on a row of periodically modulated corrugated metallic strips. The odd-mode SSPP structure can realize radiation at lower frequencies. The non-uniform corrugated metallic strips can convert SSPP to radiating waves at higher frequencies. The simulated results exhibit that the proposed antenna has two operational bands. The end-fire radiation is obtained at low band (2.28 - 2.95 GHz) and frequency beam-scanning properties is realized at high band (4.7 - 5.0 GHz). Due to this antenna low profile, wideband and low cost, it could be a candidate for planar integrated communication systems.

articleTitle: Circularly and Linearly Polarized Planar Antenna Element with Perturbed Feeding System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a planar antenna that emits circularly/linearly polarized radiation with a perturbed feed, in which the resonant frequencies of the two antenna elements are slightly shifted. The antenna is composed of a printed dipole antenna and a planar inverted-F antenna on a dielectric substrate. The antenna is designed based on simulation results and its characteristics are experimentally verified. The results confirm that the proposed antenna radiates both circular and linear polarization.

articleTitle: A CRLH-TL Inspired Multi-Functional Metamaterial and Its Application in Reconfigurable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Composite Right/Left Handed Transmission Line (CRLH-TL) based multi-functional metamaterial is designed, which combines both Right Handed Transmission Line (RH-TL) parts and CRLH-TL parts. Two different functional reconfigurable antennas are proposed based on the same metamaterial structure. By loading PIN diodes to switch the dispersion properties of the proposed metamaterial structure, the antenna 1 has the ability to obtain pattern diversity in two bands. By using varactor diodes to continuously tune the dispersion properties, the antenna 2 can achieve dual band frequency tuning.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Location on Uniformity of Radio Wave Coverage in Rectangular Tunnels with Different Cross Section Sizes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, effect of transmitting antenna location on uniformity of radio wave coverage in tunnel is studied. Radio wave coverage is modeled by ray-tracing method. A factor named system field strength flatness factor is put forward and applied to evaluate radio wave coverage properties in tunnels. The variation laws of system field strength flatness factors with antenna positions in tunnels with different cross section sizes are compared. The results show that the uniformity of radio wave coverage is sensitive to the position of transmitting antenna. Moreover, for tunnels with different cross section sizes, the antenna layouts which generate low system field strength flatness factor are different. Conclusion of this paper can provide guidance for the antenna layouts in tunnels with different cross section sizes.

articleTitle: A 24GHz Millimeter Wave Microstrip Antenna Array for Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 24GHz millimeter wave microstrip antenna array is proposed, which consists of 6×8 elements and the feeding network. The simulation result indicates that the VSWR is lower than 1.5 from 24GHz to 24.25GHz and the maximum gain is 20.56dBi.The power radio in both E-plane and H-plane follows the exponential distribution for lower sidelobelevel(SLL). The half power beamwidth (HBPW) in the H-plane is 12.2° and the SLL is -19.1dB. In the E-plane, the HBPW is 19.2° and the SLL is -18dB. The proposed antenna has advantages of high gain and low SLL, which proves the antenna applicable in automotive radar.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation on Super-resolution Doppler Velocity Estimation Method by Gauss Kernel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Lower band ultra-wideband (UWB) radar is promising for through-wall imaging application owing to higher range resolution and deeper penetration depth. Various studies revealed that Doppler signature is indispensable for human detection, where so-called micro-Doppler component of legs or arms should be correctly estimated or separated. However, the traditional Fourier transform based Doppler analysis suffers from an inherent trade-off between Doppler and temporal resolution. In addition, the higher fractional bandwidth incurs range walk problem, which make worse for the above resolution problem. This paper focuses on the recently proposed super-resolution Doppler velocity estimation by Gaussian kernel estimator, and investigates the experimentally test, using the X-band UWB radar, whether the proposed method retains its superiority.

articleTitle: A broadband Low RCS Antenna Based on Double-layer Perfect Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A double-layers perfect metamaterial absorber (DLPMA) in the microwave frequencies is proposed to reduce the radar cross section (RCS) of the circularly polarized(CP) tilted beam antenna, and it exhibits a wider band by reducing the distance between the three absorption peaks. Absorbing characteristics are analyzed and the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed absorber works well from 5.95GHz to 6.86GHz (relative bandwidth 14.1%) with the thickness of 0.5mm. The main part of PEC ground plane for the tilted beam antenna is covered by this DLPMA. As compared with the circularly polarization tilted beam antenna with a PEC ground plane, the simulation results reveal that the monostatic RCS of the antenna is reduced significantly, the axial ratio has an improvement, and the performance of antenna is preserved simultaneously from 5.5GHz to 7GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Low Cost FR4 Wide-Band Antenna Arrays for Future 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a new dipole-slot antenna array with beam-steering characteristic and end-fire radiation beams is proposed for 28 GHz smartphone applications. Eight elements of compact dipole-slot antennas have been placed on the top region of PCB (60×120 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Another set of the 8-element linear phased array with the same performance could be used at the bottom portion. A low-cost FR-4 dielectric is used as the substrate. The antenna elements provide a broad bandwidth with more than 10 GHz while impedance matching is better than -10 dB. The proposed 5G array antenna offers good fundamental characteristics including directivity and wide-scan beam-steering function which makes it fit the need of 5G mobile terminals. Simulation validations were conducted and satisfactory results were obtained.

articleTitle: Estimation of Cloud Attenuation over Bangkok, Thailand Based on an ITU-R Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We estimated satellite signal degradation by cloud. Cloud attenuation over Bangkok, Thailand, was estimated with an International Telecommunication Union Radiocommunication sector (ITU-R) model. The estimation was done at several high frequency bands: Ku, Ka and Q/V band with a variety of antenna elevation angles at the ground station of THAICOM satellite. According to the ITU-R model, the worst possible case of cloud attenuation over Thailand in Ku band would be 0.6 dB but in V band could be up to 9 dB. In the Ka band, cloud attenuation was the worst for Singapore, followed by Japan, Thailand and Italy. This estimation scheme may benefit new developers of satellites and their ground stations.

articleTitle: A Planar Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar polarized omnidirectional antenna is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of three folded dipoles printed on PCB. The 10dB return loss bandwidth is 6%(2.39GHz~2.54GHz). It has a good omnidirectional pattern (variations within 0.16dB) in the horizontal plane. The proposed antenna is fabricated and the measured results are in good agreement with the simulated results. The antenna operates at 2.4GHz for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: A Mixed Cross Coupling Gap Waveguide Bandpass Filter with Asymmetric Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel mixed cross coupling bandpass filter based on groove gap waveguide technology. A fifth-order cross-coupled bandpass filter centered at 15.07 GHz is designed. A pair of asymmetric transmission zeros are introduced by mixed cross coupling between nonadjacent resonators, which improves the filter selectivity. A wide coupling window is designed to get a wider passband. The designed filter works at Ku band with a 4% relative bandwidth and 0.4 dB insertion loss.

articleTitle: Frequency Control of a Varactor-Loaded Dual-Band Single-Layer Shorted Multi-Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by an L-probe with Reduced Patch Area in Half
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents measured frequency-tunable performance of a varactor-loaded dual-band shorted multi-ring microstrip antenna (MR-MSA) fed by an L-probe with reduced patch area in half. The proposed varactor-loaded MR-MSAs consist of multiple ring patch elements arranged concentrically and an L-probe to excited the patches arranged in the same layer with a single-layer dielectric substrate. Two varactor diodes are mounted on each ring patch where a current on the patch is maximized. Bias circuits to supply a DC bias voltage to the varactor diodes on each patch are placed on the backside of the ground with another dielectric substrate. Resonant frequencies of the ring patches can be controlled electronically by the DC bias voltages applied to the varactor diodes almost independently. In order to miniaturize the ring patches, a varactor-loaded single-layer shorted MR-MSA with reduced patch area in half is proposed. Two shorted vias situated at the center of the ring patch can remove the area of the ring patch in half. Furthermore, one of the two separated patches can be removed. Therefore, the patch area of the proposed frequency-tunable MR-MSA is reduced by a quarter in comparison with the original one. In this paper, the proposed miniaturized varactor-loaded frequency-tunable MR-MSA for dual-band operation is designed and tested. Measured frequency-tunable ranges of the two resonant frequencies of the test antenna are 2.614 to 3.347 GHz for the first mode and 3.446 to 4.535 GHz for the second mode, which are corresponding to fractional bandwidths of 24.6% and 26.7%, respectively. Although measured gain of the test antenna is reduced due to the miniaturization, excellent frequency-tunable performance as well as stable radiation patterns is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Planar Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Complementary Antenna for Endfire Radiation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar reconfigurable circularly polarized (CP) complementary antenna for endfire radiation is proposed. A quarter wavelength shorted microstrip patch and a pair of half wavelength printed electric dipole are combined to radiate endfire CP electromagnetic waves. Four PIN diodes are introduced to form two polarization states, which are left hand circularly polarized (LHCP) and right hand circularly polarized (RHCP). The simulated results show that the proposed antenna can switch between LHCP and RHCP and have stable performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-polarized Broadband Feed for the Compact Range Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel compact dual-polarized 2-18 GHz quadruple-ridged horn used as feed in a compact range is presented. A ridge profile based on the exponential and Bessel curves is proposed to improve the feed horn radiation patterns at higher frequencies and to shorten the horn axial length. The designed horn is fabricated and measure, and measured results demonstrate that the horn provides symmetrical radiation patterns, larger than 12° and 8.3° -1 dB beam-width in the E-plane and H-plane, respectively, low voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of smaller than 1.8, high port-to-port isolation (> 30dB), over the entire operation band of 2-18 GHz. The axial length of the designed horn is 8.8 cm, and the side length of the aperture is 11 cm. The presented quadruple-ridged horn which also has the features of dual linear polarization and easy excitation is most suitable to be a feed for the compact range application.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Kurtosis-Based FastICA and RobustICA Using Spatial Smoothing Preprocessing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Independent Component Analysis (ICA) is expected to decompose the incident signals and detect each signal effectively and conveniently. ICA is a statistical technique utilizing only the property that incident signals are independent of each other. This paper discusses an improved method to introduce spatial smoothing preprocessing (SSP) into FastICA and RobustICA algorithms.

articleTitle: Design of a high-selectivity lowpass-wideband bandpass diplexer using microstrip structure of loaded lumped-element
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel diplexer with enhanced selectivity is proposed. The diplexer is composed of a lowpass filter and a bandpass filter, where the size of the low-pass channel is decreased by lumped-element and the bandwidth of the bandpass channel is expand by using cross-coupled stepped-impedance resonator (SIR). The selectivity of wideband bandpass channel is enhanced by a spurious response on lowpass channel's stopband. The diplexer's design method is proposed in detail and have been verified by an experimental results of the fabricated diplexer. The 3dB cut-off frequency of lowpass channel is 0.84 GHz and a bandpass channel's passband is 1.15-2.0 GHz. The measured results show low insertion loss and high-selectivity, which agree well with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A design of miniaturized Vivaldi antenna for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, a stripline fed Vivaldi antenna with more than 7:1 bandwidth is presented. With tapered slot edges and resonant cavity, the presented antenna has the capacity to extend the low-end bandwidth limitation and improve the radiation characteristics in the lower frequencies. In addition, rectangular patches are stuck on the antenna in the flare edge to enhance the antenna's radiation. The simulated results show that good radiation patterns with gain 1.6 to 9.9 dBi in the end-fire direction could be achieved in the whole working band, which covers 1.32GHz to 9.88GHz (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> ≤ -10dB). Due to its good radiation performance of the proposed antenna, it can be used for ultra-wideband systems which work in S and C bands.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized One-Dimensional Phased-Array Antenna in X-Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The difficulty of double-polarized one-dimensional phased-array antenna with large-angle scanning is to realize two differently polarized radiating elements in the interval of nearly half wavelength. In the X-band, the spacing should be controlled within 17 mm. Under the technical requirements of power, efficiency and environment, based on the comparison of microstrip oscillator, SIW slot, waveguide slot and single-ridge waveguide slot, it is determined that a double-polarized antenna row element consisting of the single-ridge waveguide broad-wall slot with vertically polarized waves and rectangular waveguide narrow-wall slot with horizontally polarized waves realizes a one-dimensional scanning of phased array on the vertical. The computer-aided method is used to calculate the active admittance in the crack and the gap conductance function. Finally, the feasibility of the design is verified by electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of DOA Estimation Using Compressed Sensing by SAGE Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Compressed sensing can estimate the directions-of- arrival (DOAs) of radio waves with one snapshot. This paper proposes a new method in which FISTA and SAGE algorithm are combined effectively. The DOA estimation accuracy of the proposed method is evaluated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Generation of Multiple OAM Modes Using Time-Modulated Concentric Circular Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The method of generating multiple orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes using time-modulated concentric circular arrays (TMCCAs) is proposed and analyzed. TMCCAs consist of RF-switch-controlled elements located on multiple concentric rings. Unlike conventional concentric phased arrays, TMCCAs introduce the phase shift required for vortex waves by periodically energizing elements with RF switches. Results show that TMCCAs can simultaneously generate multiple OAM modes at harmonic frequencies.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Patch Array Antenna with Stable Beam for 77 GHz Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 2×8 patch array fed by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) transverse slots was proposed for 77 GHz automotive radar applications. It is a multilayer structure which can be fabricated by printed circuit board (PCB) processing. Four 2×2 sub-arrays were linearly arranged and fed by a symmetrical SIW feeding network with excitation port in the middle space. stable beams in both xoz- and yoz-plane can be achieved benefiting from the symmetry of the feeding network. Good agreement between the simulation and measurement validates the correctness of this design. The proposed low-weight low-cost array antenna possesses an operation frequency band of 5%, a maximum gain of 15.8 dBi, an orthogonal polarization discrimination higher than 30 dB, a profile of 0.137λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, etc.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Various Double Loops Frequency Selective Surfaces in terms of Angular Stability
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the comparison of Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) structure performance based on three different double loops: square, circular and hexagonal structures. The simulation process of the double loops FFS structures are carried out by using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio software. The dielectric substrate used in the simulation is the FR-4 lossy substrate (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=4.3). The simulation results show that the frequency resonated at 11.13 GHz (BW = 2.37 GHz), 11.06 GHz (BW = 2.29 GHz) and 11.07 GHz (BW = 2.25 GHz) for the double square loops, double circular loops, and double hexagonal loops FSS structures, respectively. Although the square loop structure is known to have the best filtering performance; however, based on this study, it is proven that the hexagonal and circular structures have better performance in terms of angular stability. The resonant frequency deviation for both the double hexagonal loops and double circular loops is approximately 5 % for TE mode and 1 % for TM mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Cross Polarization Compensation Feed for Single Offset Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented a multimode feed with novel chute corrugation for single offset parabolic reflector antennas, which is conjugate matched and uses novel chute corrugation. With three asymmetrical cylinders inserted, higher order mode TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> is introduced into the horn in addition to the fundamental HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode. Then adjusting TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> mode with proper amplitude and phase and the cross polarization caused by the offset structure has been dramatically reduced in asymmetrical plane of secondary radiation pattern. The electric fields of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> mode at the aperture of the multimode horn and cross polarization of the reflector illuminated by the conventional horn are plotted to observe their similarity. Finally, the expected propagation performance and the cross polarization reduction are obtained, and the designed horn is easy to manufacturing and fabricate because of its simple and reliable structure.

articleTitle: Latin Hypercube Sampling and Support Vector Regression-Assisted Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Targets
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reliable and efficient analysis of electromagnetic scattering from targets is important for target recognition and stealth design. In this paper, a method combining sampling design with machine learning is proposed. Latin hypercube sampling is adopted to sample backscattering data in hopes of improving sampling efficiency, and support vector regression (SVR) is utilized to train the model so as to obtain an efficient and accurate nonlinear regressor. With the aid of multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM), the feasibility of the proposed method is validated by the simulation data of a SLICY model. It also shows the potential of sampling design in analysis of electromagnetic scattering from a complex target.

articleTitle: Characteristics Analysis of Two Slots on a Metal Case with an Inside Folded Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In wireless communication devices, efficient arrangement of antennas is required along with the miniaturization of devices. On the other hand, from the viewpoint of heat resistance etc., it is necessary to mount an antenna inside a metal case instead of resin or plastic. However, if the antenna is completely surrounded by metal, it will not radiate for the communication. In this paper, we consider that maintaining the communication of the IoT device installed in the metal case by loading a folded dipole antenna in the metal case of the IoT device with two slots.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband Dual-polarized Array Based on Three-Dimensional SIW Feeding for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband dual-polarized array based on three-dimensional (3-D) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed for 5G millimeter-wave (MMW) applications. The array consists of printed log-periodic dipole arrays (PLPDA) as the radiating element and a 3-D SIW structure as the feeding network. Based on 3-D topology, the SIW network is composed of two vertical and one horizontal feeding networks, realizing the flexible energy spatial transfer and dual-polarized radiation. Simulated results indicate that the impedance bandwidth is great than 37% (22-32GHz). In addition, an average gain of 10.1 dBi and 10 dBi are obtained with high port isolation for both ports. Meanwhile, stable radiation patterns with low cross-polarization throughout the operating band is also achieved. Wide operating band, high gain performance and high port isolation make the proposed array attracting in MMW applications.

articleTitle: Single-layer high-gain planar lens antenna based on the Focusing Gradient Meta-surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single-layer transmitting focusing gradient meta-surface (FGMS) has been designed, which is used in the application of the lens antenna. The element of FGMS is composed of two identical structures mounted on the top and bottom surface of one dielectric layer, which can achieve high transmitting efficiency and sufficient phase compensation in X band. The antennas are placed the focus of FGMS to develop a flat lens antenna system. The simulation results demonstrate that the lens achieves a gain of 16.9 dBi and achieves 8.9 dB higher than the bare patch antenna at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Low-Profile Quasi-Yagi Antenna Using Artificial Magnetic Conductor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband low-profile quasi-Yagi antenna operating above a metal surface is presented in this paper. The design approach combines a printed double-element quasi-Yagi antenna and an Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) reflector, which can eliminate the negative effect of the metal on the antenna performance, such as impedance mismatch and low radiation efficiency. To verify the design, a prototype of the antenna is fabricated and the performance of the antenna, such as reflection coefficient and radiation pattern, are studied.

articleTitle: Membrane Patch Anetnna Array with Inflatable Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a P-band membrane patch antenna array with inflatable cavity, which is to be used to construct huge aperture antenna on a platform with limited load capacity. This type of antenna array has low density of 0.6kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and can easily conformal to the platform. Relevant measures have been introduced to reduce gross weight of the antenna array. Experimental results of this antenna array meet the weight and initial design requirements.

articleTitle: A Source Reconstruction Technique Using Eigenmode Currents
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Diagnosis of array antennas is one of the biggest challenging problems. Source reconstruction of array antennas is a promising technique for diagnosis of array antennas. However, it is well known that conventional source reconstruction techniques suffer from ill-conditioned nature of problems under study. In this paper, a novel source reconstruction technique based on eigenmode currents of the antenna under study (AUT) is applied to diagnosis of array antennas. It is clarified that the number of eigenmode currents for source reconstruction should be reduced to a moderate value in order to alleviate ill- conditioned nature of the problems under study.

articleTitle: Micro-Drone Detection with FMCW Radar Based on Stationary Point Concentration Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper shows an interesting detection performance of frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar. We challenge to detect a micro-drone whose size is about a little finger. Applying the stationary point concentration (SPC) technique, we overcome the inherent problem of leakage in the FMCW radar and set a new record for ultra-small drone detection. The SPC technique attenuates the phase noise of the leakage, and this leads to the reduction of the noise floor in the power spectrum. Therefore, we can expect to detect the beat signal of the micro-drone buried in the noise floor due to its extremely small radar cross section. Experimental results demonstrate that the noise floor is significantly reduced, and the micro-drone buried in the noise floor is detected well.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional SIW Slot Doublet Antenna for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An omnidirectional slot doublet antenna based on the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is designed, simulated and implemented in this work. The proposed antenna is composed of an SIW slot doublet antenna and SIW-microstrip tapered transition, which has a compact structure and features good omni-directivity in 5G millimeter waveband. The maximum gain of the antenna is 0.94 dBi and the E plane out-of-roundness is 2.5dB at 28GHz. The designed antenna is ideal for element of 5G multiple input multiple output (MIMO) mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Analysis of 2 × 2 Radiating Slots with Parallel-Plate Perpendicular-Corporate Feed Based on Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An analysis of 2 × 2 radiating slots with parallel-plate perpendicular-corporate feed is presented based on the method of moments. The radiating slots are wide so that both the longitudinal and the transverse magnetic currents on the slots have been taken into account in the analysis. The application of Garlekin's method together with dyadic Green's functions expanded by eigenmodes requires much less analysis time of the model, comparing with that by a commercial software based on finite element method. The reliability of the method has been verified by HFSS, the frequency characteristic of the reflection has demonstrated good accuracy.

articleTitle: Radio Wave Visualizer for 5G New Radio Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The wavelengths of the high-frequency bands under consideration for the 5th generation mobile communication systems (5G) are much shorter than those used previously, and these bands are greatly affected by people, vehicles, and other objects in the vicinity of terminals such as mobile phones. Considering this, we enhanced previously developed equipment that provides a 360° real-time visualization of fluctuations in the state of arriving radio waves from a 3rd Generation Partnership Project compliant 5G base station due to such effects. This newly developed equipment considers the New Radio specification and enables us to confirm easily the number of arriving radio waves, to orient antennas appropriately, and optimize cell planning.

articleTitle: Omni-directional High Gain Dipole Array Antenna for WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A planar high gain dipole array dual-frequency WIFI(Wireless Fidelity) antenna with Omni-directional radiation patter in the horizontal plane has been proposed in this paper, which is composed of the unequal splitter and unevenly distributed 1×3 dipole array. The width of the antenna is reduced without much affecting other antenna performance by using half of the symmetric structure in the y direction. The size of the antenna is 180 × 12.5 × 0.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The impedance bandwidths, determined from VSWR ≤ 2.0, can reach about 15.2/14.8% from 2341-2727/5087-5900 MHz covering the proposed WLAN operating bands. For the lower band(2400-2500GHz)/higher band(5150-5850MHz), the peak gain is greater than 5.6/7dBi and the efficiency is greater than 79/60%. Omnidirectional radiation characteristic in the horizontal plane is acceptable.

articleTitle: Research on an Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Array for 5G Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Vivaldi antenna is a good performance tapered slot antenna, which is widely used in design and application of planar ultra wide band antennas. In theoretical research, the spread bandwidth of the Vivaldi antenna can be loaded to infinity. However, in actual processing and manufacturing, the gain is affected by the processing technology and the size of antennas. Based on the classic Vivaldi antenna, this paper effectively increases the main lobe gain and reduces the side lobes by media culling , adding pencil-type slots and adding a parallel 1×8 feed network. Eventually the array resonates at 38GHz and the gain of the array at 38GHz reaches 13.6dB. Although the size of the antenna unit is slightly larger , which results in the radiation pattern main lobe of the array splitting, the size reduction of Vivaldi antennas will lead to gain decreasing, so the gain is similar to a smaller array without a splitting. Considering the simplicity of manufacture, this design is more cost performance.

articleTitle: A Dual Band/Dual Polarization Compact Feed Chain for Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a dual band/dual polarization compact feed chain for Satellite Communication Applications. The system operates in receiving and transmitting k/ka band with polarization diversity, achieving the right-and left-hand circular polarization in each band. The chain consists an OMJ, four low-pass filters, a turnstile power divider, two septum polarizers, and a corrugated horn. Over the whole Rx and Tx bands, the return loss is less than -30dB. Axial ratio on axis is below 0.35 dB. Between Rx and Tx ports, isolation is higher than 100 dB in both bands. The port-port isolation is higher than 18 dB.

articleTitle: Topological Transformation OAM Based on Metasurface Generated Bessel Beam
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Metasurfaces have provided new opportunities to control electromagnetic waves, which may find applications in areas such as wireless communications, imaging, energy harvesting, and invisible cloaks. Among all of the applications, Bessel beams and orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams have been investigated extensively. The combination of Bessel beam and OAM can engender some interesting phenomenon. In this work, we report a topological transformation of mode in the transmission of OAM using millimeter wave metasurface. Unit cell of the metasurface is designed to adjust phase of the transmitted wave. Two kinds of Bessel beams carrying OAM are encoded simultaneously with a crossed arrangement. Simulation results show that with the propagation of the beam, the mode number of OAM transformed from one to four and the energy delivered to all four modes. This work may be helpful in the transportation exploring of OAM and can be used in multifunction wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Dual-frequency Broadband Patch Antenna with L-shaped Probe Feed for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band broadband patch antenna with an L-shaped probe feed is proposed for 5G communication. The two frequency bands of the patch antenna are 2.51 GHz - 2.66 GHz and 3.06 GHz - 4.2 GHz, respectively, achieved more than 30% of the bandwidth and an average gain of 5 dBi in the second frequency band. The actual measurement of the antenna shows that the numerical simulation analysis of the target antenna is consistent with the measurement results, meeting the requirements of miniaturization and wideband of the 5G communication antenna.

articleTitle: The research on critical frequency of F2 layer variations during low solar activity period near the equatorial anomaly crest region in China
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we use the critical frequency of F2 layer (foF2) data of two ionosonde observation stations in Guangzhou and Haikou to analyze the variation of foF2 during the low solar activity period from January 2005 to December 2007. In this study, we analyzed the daily variation, seasonal variation and its variation with low solar activity, and the effects of space weather events such as magnetic storm on foF2. The diurnal variation of foF2 shows a minimum before the sunrise, then rises steadily with time, and the maximum occurs near 16:00 local time in the afternoon. The mean diurnal variations during different seasons are brought out. It is found that foF2 is at its maximum during Equinoctial months (March, April, May, September, October, November), and minimum during the summer months (June, July, August), with intermediate values during Winter months (December, January, February), showing a semi-annual variation. Besides, foF2 at spring equinox is larger than it at autumn.
