Overall foF2 decreases since 2005, onwards showing a positive correlation with solar activity. foF2 variations during the geomagnetic storm commencing 24 August 2005 with Dst=-184nT are analysed. foF2 shows a positive ionospheric storm effect on the first day of the storm and negative ionospheric storm effect on the next day.

articleTitle: Beam-Steerable Dual-Circular Polarized 60 GHz Patch Antenna Array With 8×8 Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A beam-steerable dual-circular polarized 60 GHz patch antenna array is proposed in this paper. A 1×4 dual-fed stacked patch antenna array is integrated with a 8×8 Butler matrix. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna array satisfies a -10 dB reflection coefficient over the frequency range of 59.5 GHz - 68.4 GHz. The proposed array has a beam-steering capability with the maximum gain of 11.4 dBi and generates the dual-circular polarization simultaneously.

articleTitle: Computation Time-Domain Far Field of a Helical Antenna above the Lossy Half-space
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the analytical expressions of the timedomain far field for arbitrarily oriented dipole above half-space are derived, which include the convolution of incident wave sources and time-domain reflection coefficient. The time-domain reflection coefficient is obtained by the time-domain propagating mode method. The time-domain far field of complex antenna can be obtained by the superposition principle. Finally, the transient radiation field of a helical antenna above the lossy half-space is calculated.

articleTitle: A Novel De-Noising Method for GPR Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: De-noising of target echo has attracted plenty of attention in better identification of target signals for ground penetrating radar (GPR). In this paper, a novel de-noising method for GPR signal is proposed. By adding LMS (Least Mean Square) adaptive filtering into wavelet threshold algorithm, both threshold processing of the high-frequency coefficients and filtering of the low-frequency coefficients are realized. Simulation result shows that the proposed joint de-noising method has better signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and root mean square error (RMSE) compared with the performance of traditional wavelet threshold de-noising method.

articleTitle: Indoor Human Tracking with Millimeter-Wave Minimum Redundancy MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Array radar needs enough array length to realize high angular resolution. However, it takes cost to increase elements physically. Recently, Minimum Redundancy Multiple- Input Multiple-Output (MR-MIMO) was proposed to increase the number of virtual elements efficiently. Further improvements by using Khatri-Rao (KR) transformation in the case of incoherent waves were also proposed. In this paper, we show experimental results on indoor human tracking with millimeter-wave MR- MIMO radar to verify the improvements of resolution and tracking performance in comparison with the results by a conventional MIMO radar.

articleTitle: The investigation of toroidal dipole resonance based on terahertz metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: we proposed a planar terahertz metasurfaces composed of asymmetric split rings resonators on polyimide substrate. Simulation results show that three resonances are observed in the transmission spectrum, and stronger toroidal dipole resonances are obtained at 0.29 THz and 1.25THz. The electromagnetic characteristics would be tuned by the parameters of the width of metal bar.

articleTitle: Recent Isolation Enhancement Techniques Applied to Array Antenna Design for 5G Sub-6GHz Band Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this invited paper, a brief discussion on recent development in isolation improvement techniques applied to antenna designs for 5G sub-6GHz band smartphone applications is presented. Here, we will begin by introducing the various factors that are affecting the isolation between two antenna elements in close proximity, follow by introducing the recent MIMO array antenna designs with single and dualband characteristics and their applied isolation techniques applied and performances.

articleTitle: Broadband asymmetric metal-traps-loaded open-sleeve dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An asymmetric open-sleeve dipole antenna with metal-trap-loaded is designed for realizing the omnidirectional pattern in a wide bandwidth. The dipole antenna is consisted of two radiator bodies, where the upper arm is two trapezoidal cross-planes each of which is loaded with two metal strips, and the coaxial feeding outer conductor is used as the lower radiator arm which is connected by shorting open-sleeve. The metal-strap-loaded is utilized to optimize the reverse currents which deteriorate the radiation pattern of asymmetric dipole antenna. Meanwhile, in order to improve the wide range of operating bandwidth, the grounded open-sleeve and top-loaded technologies are also used the design of the antenna. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna operates in the frequency band of 2.4-6 GHz with a return loss of less than -10 dB and the gain varies from 0.6-1.96 dBi.

articleTitle: The localization of the capsule endoscopy with the transmit and receive antennas for WPT
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, a capsule endoscopy has been used as one of the medical devices that can diagnose small intestines painlessly. Wireless power transmission (WPT) to the capsule endoscopy has been studied, and the efficiency of the WPT can be improved by using location information of the capsule. In the previous research, a localization method for the WPT to the capsule was developed in simulation. The purpose of this paper is to investigate whether the localization method can be applied to the localization of the capsule with the transmit and receive antennas for the WPT. We evaluated the algorithm developed in the previous research, so that the effectiveness of the algorithm was shown.

articleTitle: Target Identification in Traffic Monitoring Using Millimeter-Wave FM-CW Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, target identification by millimeter-wave radar has been studied for Traffic monitoring systems. Doppler frequency is one of the key parameters for target identification by radar. Time-frequency analysis can be performed by applying short-time Fourier transform to radar data, thereby we can see difference of periodicity in Doppler frequency. However, it is difficult to distinguish small or no periodicity targets such as bicycles and cars. In this paper, we show spectrogram for each target by applying short-time Fourier transform in slow time direction to experimental data acquired by millimeter-wave FM-CW radar. Then we show that target identification can be done by calculating mean and standard deviation of target velocity.

articleTitle: Hybrid Planar Absorber: Towards a compact absorber
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design and realization of a hybrid electromagnetic absorber combining a natural absorbing material, based on epoxy foam loaded with millimetric carbon fibers, and an artificial resonant absorber, based on metamaterial unit cells. Two studies were conducted in parallel, the first was focused on the optimization of a planar multilayer absorber using the genetic algorithm and the gradient of impedance principle, and the second was focused on the design and optimization of a metamaterial to broaden the band of absorption. A significant reduction of the total thickness (by 70%) was obtained for the final hybrid absorber while maintaining the same absorption performance.

articleTitle: Design of Microwave Power Detection Module for L-Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Microwave power measurement has an important academic and commercial value in many areas such as radar, remote sensing of environment and satellite communication. In view of L-band used in satellite communication, this paper proposes a novel design of a microwave power detection module. The power detecting range is from -60dBm to -20dBm, and covers the frequency from 900MHz to 2200MHz. The frequency resolution is 5MHz.

articleTitle: The Design of a Duplex Feed Antenna in SATCOM on-the-Move System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In traditional satellite communication, fixed position communication base station can guarantee static real-time communication to satellite, but can not guarantee it in motion, and the SATCOM on-the-move system can solve this problem. Aiming at the mobile satellite ground station communication system and realizing the duplex communication of the whole system, this paper designs a corrugated horn duplex feed with waveguide duplexer applied to the SATCOM on-the-move system at Ku band. The frequency bands of this feed antenna are 12.25 -12.75GHz and 14.0- 14.5GHz, respectively (Typical frequency of Ku-band satellite communication). The reflection coefficient of waveguide duplexer is lower than -18dB, and the reflection coefficient of this duplex feed is lower than -15dB. The out-band suppression is greater than 95dB.

articleTitle: The Optimum Design of A 3-10GHz Linear-polarized Fragmented Aperture Array with Integrated Balun
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A linear-polarized fragmented aperture array operating over 3-10GHz is presented. The array element uses an integrated balun proposed in the planar ultrawideband modular antenna (PUMA) array, without external balun or hybrid. The array element is optimized using the embedded genetic algorithm (GA) toolbox of MATLAB together with the software Ansoft HFSS. The simulated VSWR in the whole operating frequency band is less than 3. The cross-polarization level in the E-plane is lower than that of the H-plane. Cross-polarization levels remain more than 15dB below the co-polarization out to 60° for both planes.

articleTitle: On the Modeling of a DC Motor in Electric Vehicle’s EMC Studies
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the feasibility of replacing the motor system of an electric vehicle in numerical simulations by a monopole or dipole antenna model is studied and reported. Modeling results indicate that, both the monopole and dipole replacement with properly chosen lengths can similarly resemble the actual motor’s radiation characteristics. Either of these two approaches can thus be adopted in modeling studies.

articleTitle: A E-band Cavity-Backed Patch Antenna Fed by Compact SIW for ADAS Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband Cavity-Backed patch antenna using a substrate-integrated waveguide aperture-coupled feeding for E- band ADAS radar is proposed in this paper. This antenna comprises four layers stacked on top of one another and consist of three substrate layers. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth(S11<-10dB) of the antenna is from 75.77 GHz to 85.50 GHz. The maximum gain in the bandwidth is 7.4 dBi, and the radiation efficiency can be kept above 96%. The antenna is small in size, easy to manufacture, and convenient to form an array. The antenna proposed in this paper has broad application prospects for autonomous driving, vehicle networking and ADAS system.

articleTitle: Drone Detection with Linear Chirp Pulse Radar using Coherent Pulse Integration
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the detection of small drone with linear chirp pulse radar system. The system employs 14.1GHz as RF center frequency with bandwidth 200MHz to cover Linear Chirp Pulse (LCP) whose chirp rate is 80MHz. The LCP is radiated and received through quasi-monostatic antennas with the gain of 16dBi. The system also includes digital down converter to obtain IQ signal from LCP received at RX antenna. Finally, Matched filtering of the LCP is performed to maximize the SNR of the signal reflected from the drone. In the actual performance measurement, the drone signal was detected up to 400m distance in real-time using Coherent Pulse Integration (CPI). The raw data is obtained as csv file and then later processed with MATLAB.

articleTitle: A Novel Wideband Circular Patch Antenna With Conical Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this contribution, a novel ultra-wideband antenna with conical radiation pattern is proposed and discussed in detail. This antenna is intended to operate in the frequency range from 4 GHz to 7.8 GHz. With the combination of a circular patch, conical cavity and feeding, the antenna provides a wide bandwidth and conical radiation pattern. The operation principle of the antenna has been presented. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna yields an impedance bandwidth (VSWR <; 2.0) of 131.3% for the conical beam is from 3.35 GHz to 16.18 GHz, but the radiation pattern of the antenna is split between 7.8 GHz and 16 GHz. The cone radiation pattern of the antenna has no side lobes between 3.35 GHz and 7.8 GHz (79.8%), and the maximum gain is greater than 6 dBi in the frequency band. Moreover, a cone metal is added to improve the impedance bandwidth. The proposed antenna has a low profile, low cost and high power capacity to be suitable for ultra-wideband (UWB) system.

articleTitle: Design of Sector-beam Microwave Antennas using Metallic Compound Air-fed Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel kind of high gain sector-beam antenna using metallic compound air-fed array (M-CAFA) has been proposed and analyzed in this paper. By adopting slotted metal plate as partial reflective surface (PRS) cover, stepped metal g round as base and side-wall, and open ended waveguide as feed, such antenna employs fully metallic structure. Thus, it will be suitable for microwave and millimeter-wave applications exhibiting advantages of low feeding loss and low cost. A sample of sector-beam microwave antenna working at 13GHz has been presented with detailed theoretical analysis and parametric study. The optimized simulation obtains a sector beam of 32o in horizontal and 8o in vertical, peak gain of 17.5 dBi at central frequency, and return loss less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband Dual-Polarized Antenna for Base Station
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dual-polarized antenna for base station is proposed. The antenna consists of a reflector, a horizontal radiating patch, two Y-shaped feeding structures and two coaxial cables. To increase the resonance modes, a nonuniform coupling chamfer is introduced. The bandwidth is widened by improving the shape of the edge of the antenna and etching the U-shaped slot. The size of the antenna is 49.5mm×49.5mm. The antenna was manufactured and tested. The measured results show that the antenna operates from 1.7GHz to 3.7GHz with VSWR<; 2 (about 74.07%), covering 2G band (1710MHz-1920MHz) 3G band (1880MHz-2170MHz) LTE band (2300MHz-2400MHz & 2570MHz-2690MHz) and 5G band (3300MHz-3600MHz). A stable pattern and gain are achieved simultaneously in the entire operating band.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Reconfigurable Complimentary Electric-LC (CELC) Metamaterial Element
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A high-efficiency reconfigurable metamaterial element for coding holographic antennas, consisting of a complimentary electric LC (CELC) resonator, is proposed in this paper. The low efficiency problem of a traditional reconfigurable CELC element is demonstrated in terms of the power dissipation, before the structure introduction of the proposed element. Simulation showed that the proposed element has a lower ohmic loss when it is switched on, at least 20 times less than that of traditional one, thus increasing the efficiency.

articleTitle: A Research of Fuzzy Adaptive Extended Kalmal Filter Based on GPS Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper provides a fuzzy adaptive extended Kalman filter (FAEKF) based on the Global Position System (GPS), contrast with the conventional extended Kalman filter (EKF) , it shows that this algorithm can suppress filter divergence and robustness effectively from simulation experiments. FAEKF can make the receiver work properly when the noise gets bigger and changer dramatically, but conventional EKF cannot . It shows that this filter algorithm can adapt to the change of noise environments.

articleTitle: Waveform-Driven Array for MIMO Systems Operating in Complicated Scattering Environments
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Most phased arrays are predesigned assuming that they work in free space or at a high altitude. In fact, these arrays are installed near ground. The nearby obstacles or buildings on the ground may bring about negative impacts on the arrays and lead to unexpected performance degradation in the radiation such as beam distortion and gain loss. In order to address the scattering issues, here we develop a waveform-driven antenna array whose scanning beams are manipulated by different waveforms of the excitation signals rather than shifting their phases. The temporal waveforms of excitation are elaborately designed by time-reversal based beam synthesis method. The numerical simulations demonstrate that the waveform-driven array exhibits an excellent performance in dealing with severe scattering effects to achieve accurate control of beam scanning.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized Dipole Antenna for 5G New Frequency Band Base Station
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Aiming at the application of 5G base station, this paper presents a broadband miniaturized dual-polarization antenna in the form of printed dipole. The main structure of the antenna consists of two pairs of annular dipoles, and the impedance bandwidth and isolation can be effectively improved by loading impedance matching cylinder on the dipole terminal and cutting grooves on the dipole arm. Meanwhile, the miniaturization of the antenna can be effectively realized. The antenna adopts the form of coupling feed. Simulation results shows that the antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 46.8% with S11<; -10 dB (2.68 to 4.32 GHz) and a high isolation of greater than 27dB within the bandwidth. Also, a stable radiation pattern with the maximum half-power beamwidth of 69.6° at horizontal plane and a stable gain of 9.3 dBi are obtained simultaneously over the working frequency band.

articleTitle: A Broadband and Wide Angle Coverage Linear Eplane Array with Low Gain Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel broadband and wide angle coverage nine-element linear array in the E-plane is presented. A board-band and broad-beam circular patch antenna element having the dimensions of 45mm×45mm×1.8mm is used as the basic element for array design. The scanning coverage of the proposed array is from -75° to +75° at the central frequency of 3.5 GHz. The less degradation in the gain is realized when the array scans to higher angles, which is about 1.8 dB. For the isolation enhancement between the two adjacent elements of an array antenna, rectangular slots of the length λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/2 are introduced in the ground plane, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength of free space at central frequency of 3.5 GHz. The broad-beam characteristic of a single element antenna and significant isolation enhancement between nearby elements of antenna array helps in the improvement of gain and coverage efficiency of the proposed nine-element array.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Antenna Utilizing Slotline-CPW-Tapered-slot Transition
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A simple design for a compact ultra-wideband (UWB) slot antenna utilizing slotline-coplanar waveguide(CPW) -tapered slot transition is presented. By using the slotline-CPW-tapered-slot transition, both ultra-wideband characteristic and endfire directional radiation patterns are obtained. To verify the design, the simulated transient electric field distributions on the 2-D metal layer are showed. Simulated results demonstrate that a wide impedance bandwidth of 5.99 : 1 (2.63 - 15.75 GHz about 143%) under the condition of the VSWR <; 2 is achieved. The peak gains versus frequencies vary from 1.5 dBi to 5.5 dBi covering the entire UWB (3.1-10.6 GHz) with a floating of no more than 4 dB. Besides, endfire directional radiation patterns in a wide band are well maintained.

articleTitle: Fast Anisotropic Metasurface Analysis in FDTD using Surface Susceptibility Model
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The FDTD methods combined with Surface Susceptibility Model (FDTD-SSM), compared to traditional brute force metasurface simulation, have been proved efficient and accurate for fast metasurface analysis. However, the present work is limited to scattering elements that are either isotropic or that have diagonal surface susceptibilities. This paper proposes a necessary extensions of Finite Difference Time Domain equations to analyze general anisotropic metasurfaces which have off-diagonal surface susceptibility tensors. At last, the Surface Susceptibility Model simulation results are validated by geometrical structure simulation results.

articleTitle: Terminal antenna for indoor optical wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the link budget of indoor optical wireless communication by considering the gain and power of both base station (BS) and terminal antenna (UT). We calculate the relation between the BS gain and the distance of communication. And we propose a taper waveguide terminal antenna for indoor optical wireless communication.

articleTitle: Reduced-Size Crossed-Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a reduced-size crossed-dipole antenna that comprises two printed crossed-dipole arms, a ground plane, and a pair of vacant quarter printed rings to generate circularly polarized (CP) radiation. The reduced-size crossed dipole is similar to the conventional crossed dipole but differs in that half of the crossed dipole is rotated 90 degrees. By rotating half of the crossed dipole, the area covered by the conventional crossed dipole is reduced by half, resulting in a compact, small-size antenna that generates CP radiation with a performance nearly identical to that of conventional crossed dipoles in terms of axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and radiation patterns. This performance is discussed and confirmed computationally. The reduced-size crossed-dipole antenna with overall dimensions of 33 mm × 54.6 mm × 29 mm (0.269λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 0.446λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>×0.2368λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> at 2.45 GHz) has a |S11| <; -10 dB bandwidth of 2.2-2.86 GHz (26.08%), a 3-dB AR bandwidth of 2.3-2.6 GHz (12.21%), a broadside gain of 7.85-7.98 dBic, and a radiation efficiency of > 90%.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of antenna deformation for Wireless Power Transmission of Solar Power Satellite
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wireless power transmission (WPT) is one of the significant technologies towards Solar Power Satellite (SPS). Software Retrodirective method, consisting direction finding and beam forming is proposed for performing WPT. Tethered SPS has power generation and transmission panel to transmit 1 GW power. Required accuracy of WPT is 0.0005 degrees for Tethered SPS. Due to space environment, there is a concern of antenna deformation which will affect accuracy of WPT. We performed basic experiment for antenna deformation of λ/20 and λ/10. Effect of the deformation was analyzed for direction finding by measuring error of angle of arrival. Estimation was done to obtain allowable limit of position error for achieving the required accuracy.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Orthogonal Polarization Conversion Reflector Using Cross-Placed Strip Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel strip element put in the cross that is useful for orthogonal polarization conversion reflectors. Conversion efficiency is 80% in the frequency range of 14.7 GHz-43.9 GHz (the relative band is 105%). As a result, it is possible to obtain a 360° reflection phase shift by combining the proposed element with the previously developed element.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Miniaturized 24GHz FMCW Radar with High-resolution
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper addresses the design and implementation of a 24GHz FMCW radar for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) application. The radar includes one transmitter and two receivers, where the target signature can be enhanced by using two-channel data. The size of 80mm×160mm meets the requirements of miniaturization and light weight, which can be applied as mini-SAR sensor on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). The experimental results show that the front-end frequency modulated continuous wave carrier frequency is 24.25GHz, the sweep bandwidth is 700MHz, the sweep period is 600us, and the frequency deviation peak in the linear sweep is less than one thousandth of the sweep bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design of Portable Terminal Antenna for Satellite Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a portable microstrip antenna with four radiation patches. The structure of the proposed antenna is simple. The four radiation patches are fed with different phases by the coaxial feeding, the main radiation direction of the antenna can be changed, so that the antenna achieves beam-switched and covers the upper half of space. The near-field reflection coefficient, the surface field distribution and far-field radiation patterns of the antenna model verify the working mechanism of the antenna. The antenna realizes circular polarization with good axial ratio value. Test results indicate that the beam width of the antenna is wider. The gain meets requirements. The better directionality of the measured antenna can be obtained. The proposed antenna has good impedance matching and potential application value in the Tiantong satellite mobile terminal.

articleTitle: Channel Dynamics in Mobile-to-Mobile Communications: Recent Results and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recent results about mobile-to-mobile radio channel dynamics are analyzed, considering indoor peer-to-peer, body-centric and vehicule-to-pedestrian transmissions. Investigations are based on various experimental campaigns from 2.4 to 4 GHz. Regarding peer-to-peer and body-centric scenarios, measurements conducted in room-to-room and in-room environments show a strong non-stationary behavior, modeled by a Markov chain-based approach. In the vehicular context, several vehicular-to-pedestrian scenarios with different mobility patterns are investigated and channel statistics are derived.

articleTitle: An Innovative Sub-Gridding Method for Helmholtz Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An efficient finite difference sub-gridding technique has been developed. Based on this innovative sub-gridding, the discrete equations of transition nodes are constructed, which satisfy Helmholtz equation numerically. Especially for the second sort of transition nodes, their discrete equations can be not straightly relevant to other sorts of transition nodes. Theoretically, their numerical solutions are also 2-order precision. Applying this new method to solve scattering problems, the results show that the accuracy of numerical solutions is significantly improved.

articleTitle: An ultra-broadband double-layer AMC surface for RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) surface is designed for radar cross section (RCS) reduction in ultra-wide band. The proposed AMC structure is composed of two different double-layer AMC units, resulting in destructive reflection phase difference (180°±37°) in the band from 5.8 to 16.35 GHz (95.26%). Each AMC unit cell is combined by a metal patch etched on a substrate and a PEC layer, in between of which is a 2-mm-thick air gap. One of the metal patches is composed of an octagonal ring and a Union Jack cross, and the other is a circle patch. With chessboard arrangement by the two units, the RCS of the proposed surface can achieve an 91.7% (6.2-16.7 GHz) 10 dB RCS reduction bandwidth for x polarization and an 93% (6.1-16.7 GHz) bandwidth for y polarization, which demonstrates that the presented AMC surface may be found potential applications on low-RCS platforms in an ultra-wide band.

articleTitle: A Novel Microstrip Patch Antenna with Bandwidth Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel microstrip patch antenna with bandwidth enhancement is proposed in this paper. Based on the structure of the traditional microstrip patch antenna, the proposed antenna adds an impedance matching network to broaden bandwidth and achieve lower return loss. Adding a parasitic patch near the original patch, the antenna bandwidth is further expanded and the radiation characteristics of the antenna can be improved. The simulated impedance bandwidth of 16.7% (14~16.5 GHz) can be obtained and the gain in the range of bandwidth is mostly above 6 dB. The proposed antenna enjoys good impedance matching and stable gain, which make it suitable for modern communication systems, satellite communications and some control systems.

articleTitle: A Contactless Human Respiration Rate Measurement Using UWB Transversal Propagation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a transversal UWB propagation method with integrated inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors for respiration rate (RR) measurement. A custom designed platform based on the off-the-shelf UWB integrated circuit (DW1000) was used. The measurement method was developed following the assumption that the periodical changes in the lung volume during the inhale and exhale phases change the RF communication channel properties and modulate the observed received signal power. The experimental results showed that the proposed measurement method and implemented custom platform can capture reliably different breathing patterns, with an error rate within the estimated range of 10%. Taking into account that the UWB method captures not only lung motions but also the other organs, the results of varying the positions of transmitter and receiver yielded that the best places for placement of Rx and Tx UWB modules are diagonally or on the left side of the thoracic wall.

articleTitle: Analysis of Two-dimensional Beam Pointing Error of Retrodirective Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the performance of two-dimensional beam pointing error (BPE) of retrodirective array is analyzed. The effects of key parameters, including the pattern of the antenna array, the leakage of radio frequency (RF) signal and the error of amplitude and phase, on the BPE are analyzed. The simulation results show that which can be used as the theoretical evidence of the system design and performance analysis where a specifically beam pointing error are required.

Author Keywords: the error of amplitude and phase

articleTitle: Equivalent Motor Radiation of an Electric Vehicle Based on Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The feedforward neural network method is utilized in this paper for predicting the desired electromagnetic radiation properties of the motor of an electric vehicle. The neural network is first fully trained by simulation data and its predicted field values are then compared with those obtained through "traditional" FEKO simulations. The comparison has demonstrated a similar level of accuracy for both approaches, but the simulation time and cost can be dramatically reduced by employing the neural network method.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Wideband GPR Antenna with FSS-MA Shielding
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to improve the radiation bandwidth of the ground-coupled GPR antenna and the radiation performance in the preferred direction, a new wideband bowtie antenna with Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) shielding and Metamaterial Absorber (MA) is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna composed of three elements: an original bowtie antenna working at the center frequency of 1GHz, a two-sided band-stop FSS coating, and a MA. The simulation results show that the proposed FSS-MA-bowtie antenna achieves a better performance in near-field radiation, VSWR and input impedance, comparing with the original bowtie antenna. The side radiation of the original bowtie antenna is efficiently suppressed by the band-stop FSS shielding and are absorbed by back reflection. Results show that the gain of the preferred (forward) radiation direction have increased by 4dB, and the bandwidth reaches 27% by employing the FSS-MA shielding mechanism. In addition, time-domain analysis results that reflected oscillation was reduced, which satisfies the requirements of a wideband GPR system.

articleTitle: Design, Fabrication, and Measurement of Wireless Power Transmission System Based on Magnetic Resonance Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the design, fabrication, and measurement of a magnetic resonant wireless power transfer (WPT system. The proposed parallel resonant circuit power amplifier is combined with a compact wireless transceiver coil (receiving coil diameter 7 cm, transmitting coil diameter 16cm), so that the wireless power transmission system has the ability to transmit about 1 Wpower at 10 cm, and has no change in load sensitivity, and the WPT system could can receive power from LED to linear resistance. The experimental results show that the transmission efficiency of the system is as high as 42%. This article provides a novel and concise way to achieve wireless power transfer, which may help to popularize wireless charging in the future.

articleTitle: Accurate Range and Spectroscopic Data Extraction Algorithm for Dispersive Object in Terahertz-Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper focuses on an enhancement for range estimation assuming the terahertz(THz) imaging applications. The THz-band radar is promising for various applications, however, there are non-negligible range estimation errors due to frequency dependent reflection phenomena. The reflection signals from dispersive object have frequency dependent feature, then, its waveform considerably distorts from that of a reference (usually transmitted) signal. To compensate these errors, this paper introduces the wavelet based reference signal optimization. The finite difference time domain (FDTD) based numerical , assuming the THz-band radar, demonstrates the proposed method significantly enhances the range estimation at the order of 1/10 wavelength.

articleTitle: 37-42.5 GHz Sixth-Order Symmetric Substrate Integrated Waveguide Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A sixth-order symmetric Chebyshev bandpass filter applied to the 5G mobile networks is proposed in this paper. The presented BPF based the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) has low insertion loss, low cost and high selectivity. The even-order Chebyshev polynomial is modified and adopted to analysis the design of the this presented filter. This filter is designed by using a single-layer Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate with thickness of 0.254mm. The area of the presented BPF is 33.36mm ×5mm. The simulation results show that the return loss is better than 13 dB, the insertion loss is lower than 0.6 dB, the out-of-band rejection is better than 30 dB in the interval below 35.8GHz and above 46.9GHz. The results show that the proposed even-order Chebyshev polynomial is correct.

articleTitle: Internet-of-Things Sensors Wirelessly Powered by Electrically Small Huygens Dipole Rectenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensors are expected to be ubiquitous in a future smart and sustainable society. Due to the exponential growth of device numbers, powering IoT devices by far field wireless power transfer (WPT) is becoming a necessary trend. This paper introduces two IoT sensors (light and temperature) that are wirelessly powered by a highly compact and efficient electrically small Huygens dipole rectenna. The entire system seamlessly integrates two subsystems. One is the metamaterial-inspired electrically small Huygens antenna that organically combines capacitively loaded loop (CLL) and Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) radiators together. The other is the sensor-augmented rectifier in which the output DC voltage varies as a function of the sensor impedance. The developed wirelessly powered systems can sense light or temperature levels and, when attached to an alarm, can send a warning signal if a threshold value is exceeded. Their prototypes were fabricated and tested. The measured results agree very well with their simulated values. The prototypes are highly compact and electrically small (ka = 0.73). They represent ideal candidates for many emerging IoT wireless sensor applications.

articleTitle: Blind Phase Calibration by Near Field Null Detection for Linear Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a blind phase calibration by detecting near field nulls for linear array antenna. Two nulls appear in near field of a 4-element linear array and their angles are close to the position given by the array factor. Relative phase difference between two elements are found by searching their relative phase to make the null at ideal position. After calibrating two pairs of elements independently, the relative phase between two pairs is derived by an approximation formula of near field of array. We show the proposed algorism by 4-element linear array and verify it by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a Programmable Dual-Band and Dual-Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna Unit
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The development of communication systems puts forward higher demands on multi-band and multi-polarization work of antennas. In this paper, a programmable dual-band and dual-polarized microstrip patch antenna unit operating in the satellite communication frequency band is proposed. PIN diodes are introduced to control the feeding parts and realize the switch among four working states. Simulated results demonstrate the excellent performance of the proposed antenna unit providing a method to replace phase shifters and realize real-time control by automated programming.

articleTitle: Design of a Metasurface with Independent Amplitude and Phase Control
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Passive phase gradient metasurfaces are generally limited to tailoring the phase of an incident electromagnetic wave. Here, the utilization of a complementary pair of square patch and aperture on either side of a dielectric substrate has been shown to independently control the amplitude and phase of waves reflected from a metasurface. Independent amplitude and phase control is achieved by changing either the patch length or the aperture length or both the patch and aperture lengths of the metasurface unit cell. Designed metasurface can be used as an amplitude-controlled, phase-controlled or both amplitude-and phase-controlled partially reflective surface for Fabry-Perot cavity antennas.

articleTitle: Breast Tumor Characterization with Raw Data Based Machine Learning for Microwave Ultra-wideband Mammography
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Breast cancer is most diagnosed cancers for women's fatal disease in world wide. Microwave mammography is one of the most promising imaging modality, which is more safe, low cost and compact compared with X-ray based screening, and is promising for more frequently screening technique for breast cancer. This paper focuses on data based machine learning algorithm for microwave scattered data assuming ultra-wideband radar system. The advantage of our proposed method is that it directly recognize the existence or size of the tumor using unprocessed scattered data. Then, the recognition rate does not depend on the performance of preliminary signal processing or imaging algorithm. Focusing on UWB signal, multi-frequency complex data are processed via multi-layered neural network with suitable learning algorithm. The notable point of this method is that it does offer not only detection but also characterization of tumor size within 10mm scale. The 2-D and 3-D FDTD based numerical simulation, using realistic phantom, show that our method provides the recognition rate more than 80% even for less than 10mm size tumor.

articleTitle: Accuracy Assessment on the Fast PVVA Algorithm in the Beam Propagation Analysis of Quasi-Optical Beam Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, the authors report the application of the FFT-PVVA algorithm in the Quasi-Optical beam waveguide system analysis. The quasi-optical beam waveguide is generally designed based on the Gaussian beam propagation theory, and formed by quasi-optical reflectors in large electrical sizes. The FFT-PVVA algorithm takes advantages of the FFT-accelerated beam propagator and Poynting vector-based ray tracing to form a fast and accurate solution for the reflected beam modeling. In this work, the authors apply the FFT-PVVA solution to compute the reflected fields in a four mirror beam waveguide, and perform the accuracy investigation utilizing the results of physical optic integration as reference. Results show that the FFT-PVVA solution gives results with good accuracy for the propagated beam, and with superb efficiency. Also, as the modeling errors accumulate after several reflections, it is desired this solution can be further upgraded for better accuracy in future works.

articleTitle: Experimental Results of Handheld Device with 4x4 N78 Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: 4×4 N78 antennas are applied in a handheld device with LTE/GPS/Wi-Fi antennas. At 3500 MHz, all N78 antennas have good antenna efficiencies. ECCs are below 0.3 in N78 band. Throughput of different angles are above 1.54 Gbps, which is promising for 5G application.

articleTitle: Study on a VHF-band Small Loop Antenna with Adaptive Control of the Matching Circuit for Heart Rate Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Vital signs of the body are related to mental stress conditions. The variation of the R-R interval (peak-to-peak interval of the heartbeats), in particular, reflects mental stress. Non-contact detection using a Doppler sensor has been extensively studied for heart rate measurement. However, Doppler sensors are highly affected by reflections from surrounding objects or external noise, making accurate acquisition of the R-R interval difficult. To solve this problem, we propose the use of a low-radiation-efficiency VHF-band loop antenna to overcome the above problem. However, the input impedance of this antenna depends on the surrounding conditions relative to its location. In this study, we propose a sensor configuration to control the antenna impedance based on changes in the surrounding conditions, and demonstrate that the proposed configuration improves the sensor sensitivity.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Graphene-Based Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As a new two-dimensional material, graphene has been applied in various devices due to its unique electrical and optical properties. In this work, a reconfigurable Yagi antenna by using graphene's tunable conductivity is proposed. The Yagi antenna consists of one feed element and four elements which are located on either side of the feed element symmetrically. Simulated results indicate that the proposed structure achieves a good performance. Antenna works at two modes which can be tuned by changing the chemical potential of graphene. The S11, gain and efficiency are -13.47 dB, 7.56 dB and 70% while the antenna works at 2.5 GHz. It can be expected that this proposed antenna possesses potential for beam scanning in microwave devices and systems.

articleTitle: Design of Ku-band Substrate Integrated Waveguide Slot Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This letter proposes the design methods of resonant arrays of longitudinal slots in the broad wall of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). Longitudinal slots are etched on the top metallic surface of SIW. The design process and experimental results of a one-by-eight SIW slot array antenna at Ku-band are presented. The proposed 1×8 SIW slot array antenna with dimensions of 122 mm × 9mm × 0.5mm, o • ers a fractional bandwidth of 1.3% with respect to the resonance frequency of fr = 15.9GHz. At the resonance frequency of 15.9GHz, the proposed 1 × 8 SIW array antenna o • ers a gain of 13dB in the direction of normal radiation. The proposed SIW slot array antenna is simulated on ANSYS HFSS 15.0, and simulated results are verified with the fabricated proto-type.

articleTitle: A Compact Low Profile Wideband CP Antenna Using MM-TL Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design of a wideband circularly polarized (CP) antenna with a very compact size of 0.7808λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.7808λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> operating at the frequency of 2.4 GHz is presented. The antenna consists of a feeding network and four meandered monopoles on a substrate. The feeding network is designed using Wilkinson-power dividers and metamaterial transmission line (MM-TLs) to produce four output signals with equal power and sequential-phase difference of 90°. The four monopoles are placed in orthogonal positions and connected to the outputs of the feeding network to produce a CP signal. The wideband CP antenna is studied and designed using computer simulation. For verification, the antenna is also prototyped and measured using the Satimo Starlab system. The results in impedance bandwidth (IMBW), axial-ratio bandwidth (ARBW), radiation patterns and realized boresight gain are presented. Measured results show that the CP antenna has a very wide IMBW of 0.96~3.69 GHz (117.4%) and ARBW of 1.13~3.58 GHz (104.03%), which are larger than those of all designs found in literature, yet having a very compact size and low profile.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Uncertainty Evaluation in Vector Network Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We studied two approaches for S-parameter uncertainty evaluation. First approach is based on residual error model and the second is based on GUM. We obtained uncertainty results by the two approaches and compared them. We also did Monte-Carlo simulation.

articleTitle: A New Pulse Compression Technique for Distorted Chirp-Pulse Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Pulse compression, which is generally used in radar systems, is conducted using a reference signal without considering distortion which happens in systems before pulse radiation. In this paper, some methods are proposed to achieve better performance in pulse compression when a radar system is distorted. The distortion is assumed to affect three parameters; amplitude, frequency, and phase. To imitate distortion in chirp pulse form, received chirp pulses were generated with non-constant amplitude, different frequency, and different phase from the reference signal. To show the effect of the distortion on pulse compression result, pulse compression of these pulses are shown. The methods to decrease this effect include using reference signals with constant amplitude, same amplitude, and inverse form of the amplitude, respectively. To corroborate performance difference which is yielded by different reference signal forms, simulations of multiple targets is performed. In this paper, only liner FM (LFM) signal is used for simplicity.

articleTitle: Improved Near-field to Far-field Transformation for RCS and Antenna of Large Body
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The measurement for radar cross-section (RCS) of electrically large object such as airplane and for radiation pattern of large antenna are demanded strongly. We propose the improved novel near-field to far-field transformation method (NFFFT) in cylindrical scanning, from which RCS can be estimated by pickup near-field data. Our method is featured by the improved focusing factor obtained from the exact transformation integral using small spheres. This factor leads more accurate estimation for strong asymmetrical object, so that RCS measurement is available even in small anechoic chamber. In this paper, applying geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) to simple shaped models as a target, and it is shown high agreement between them and measured NFFFT results including antenna pattern. Furthermore, we discuss suppression method of unnecessary wave by imaging-area limiting.

articleTitle: Fabrication Tolerance Study of Transmission Line Resonator Based CRLH Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, the design of a transmission line (TL) resonator based composite right/left-handed (CRLH) leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) are presented. Our design utilizes bandpass filter synthesis technique to design matching sections for improving input impedance bandwidth. An LWA with a fractional bandwidth of 40% is designed. In order to discuss the sensitivity to manufacturing tolerances, simulated results of LWAs with etching variation are compared.

articleTitle: A Compact, DC Grounded Omnidirectional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact, mechanically rugged, DC grounded horizontally polarized omnidirectional antenna is proposed. The antenna is based on the coaxial cylinder structures, which consists of oversize coaxial cylinders, slots and their feeding assembly and a matching unit. The horizontal polarization property is realized by four vertical slots surrounding the axis of the coaxial cylinder in the outer conductor. The antenna is dc ground which eliminates the electrostatic discharge ESD problems. Simulation results show that the antenna bandwidth is of 8.1% (2.58GHz to 2.77 GHz), gain variation in the horizontal plane is less than ±0.5 dB while the cross-polarization level is below 46 dB over the whole bandwidth (2.58-2.77 GHz).

articleTitle: A Decoupling Method for Two PIFAs by Using Bridged Two Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we investigate a simple method to reduce the mutual coupling between two planar inverted-F antennas (PIFAs). The method shows that by using a parasitic element (PE) which is linked with a bridge line (BL) and loaded upon the PIFAs, good impedance matching and low mutual coupling around resonant frequency can be obtained without the necessity of adjusting dimensions of the PIFAs. This method is also expected to be an effective method to reduce mutual coupling of the larger PIFA arrays in future works.

articleTitle: Dual-Band FSS Director using Inverted Interdigital Structure for LTE and WLAN
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a design of dual band FSS director using inverted interdigital technique on a microwave printed circuit board to achieve resonance frequencies at 1.8 GHz for LTE and 5.2 GHz for WLAN. Form the design method, the unit cell size can be reduced from λ/2 to λ/8 compared with the conventional structure caused by the slow wave effect in its structure. The FSS layer was formed by connecting 8×8 designed unit cells to be an array. The FSS layer acts as a director for dipole antennas at the frequencies of 1.8 GHz and 5.2 GHz. The simulation results show that the dipole antenna with the proposed FSS director has higher performances. The antenna gains were obviously improved with the gains of 2.61 dB at 1.8 GHz and 3.97 dB at 5.2 GHz higher than the conventional dipole antenna, which normally has a gain of about 2 dB. This proposed FSS structure can also be applied for other multiband antenna systems.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis of Multi-Angle Bi-Static Ground Penetrating Radar Utilizing Multi-Region Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, Ground Penetrating radar is widely used to detect invisible materials such as buried objects. In the radar system, synthetic aperture radar technique is used. In the radar system, transmitting antenna and receiving antenna are used separately. In recent years, multi-angle GP-SAR is proposed to obtain more rich images. In the GP-SAR, the distance between the transmitting antenna and the receiving antenna are changed. Therefore, a lot of simulations are required to analyze multi-angle GP-SAR. In this paper, we will apply the multi-region FDTD [1] method to the GP-SAR. In the multi-region FDTD, the rotated coordinate is also used to model the oblique antenna and target.

articleTitle: Design of a Four-Port Coplanar Antenna for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A four-port coplanar antenna for Cognitive Radio (CR) applications is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna and three inner rectangular loop antennas. The UWB antenna is in charge of spectrum sensing and fully covers the UWB spectrum of 3.1 - 10.6 GHz. Three loop antennas are used for communication and cover the UWB spectrum partially. A high isolation of greater than 17.3 dB is achieved without using an additional decoupling structure.

articleTitle: Study on Passive Intermodulation Due to Metal Contact in Planar Inverted-F Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents an equivalent circuit to analyze passive intermodulation (PIM) behavior in planar inverted F antenna (PIFA). The proposed circuit model is based on a capacitance, a nonlinear resistance and an inductance in parallel connection. By theoretical analysis, metal contact area and state make a great sense on PIM level of PIFA. Measurement results show that a larger metal contact area in PIFA feeding usually has a beneficial effect on PIM performance. The methodology and experimental conclusion provide a reference method for the modeling of metal contact nonlinearity, and has considerable guiding significance for PIM suppression in mobile communication terminal products.

articleTitle: A Study on Half-shaped Printed UWB Monopole Antenna with Short Stub
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the authors propose a small planar monopole antenna corresponding to the frequency band of Ultra-wideband (UWB) system. This antenna has a structure in which a bell-shaped UWB monopole antenna formed on a dielectric substrate (FR-4) has a half shape and a short stub is loaded on the antenna. The size of the antenna is 30 × 12 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The structure is possible to operate with the frequency band of 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz even if the antenna is designed small. From the result of the frequency domain and the time domain analysis, it is shown that good characteristics can be obtained for high speed wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Circular Polarized Microstrip Planar THz Antenna Using Z-shape Slots
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper presents, the design of right hand circular polarized (RHCP), system on-chipped microstrip antenna which will be used for terahertz (THz) communication application. Z-shapes slots are used to convert the antenna from linear polarization to circular polarization. Due to the sensitive slots, the antenna will be also used for sensing application. The operating frequency range of the antenna is from 0.258-0.355 THz with 97 GHz fractional bandwidth. The operating bandwidth of the axial ratio is 11% at 3 dB. A maximum of 4.6 dBi gain is achieved at 0.26 THz frequency. Due to small amount of loss at high frequency waveguide port is used in the feeding line.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lightning induced effect on multi-core cables for ship lightning protection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: It is great harmful that lightning electromagnetic pulse environment coupling into the electronic systems for ships through cables. In this paper, we study the effectiveness of different lightning protection measures on ship cables. The ship cables with different grounding and shielding measures are injected with lightning waves according to the US military standard MIL-STD-461G, so that the circuit voltage at the end of the cables can be detected by the oscilloscope. Simulations and experiments are taken to find the optimum measures for the lightning protection.

articleTitle: Acceleration of FISTA by switching for simultaneous estimation of DOA and TOA
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper propose an acceleration method of FISTA by switching for estimation of both DOA and TOA. Numerical results show that the calculation time is reduced and estimation accuracy is also improved.

articleTitle: Decoupling of Two Dual-Band Antennas With a Reactively Loaded Dummy Element
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A decoupling technique for two closely spaced dual-band antennas using reactively loaded dummy element is presented. A double-T monopole is inserted between the two active radiators as a coupling dummy element. With the corresponding dual-band reactive load being precisely determined, the simulated port isolation can be efficiently improved to more than 30dB at 2.5/5.2GHz. The return losses of the MIMO antenna are better than 25 dB at both frequencies by cascading a three-section dual-band transformer.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Array Antenna with Built-In Filters in Multilayered LTCC Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an array antenna with a low pass filter (LPF) in LTCC multilayered substrate with low loss, high attenuation and small size in 28 GHz band. A differential feeding method for each patch antenna is employed to improve symmetricity of directivity for beam forming. The insertion loss of the LPF is less than 0.5 dB and the spurious emission in 2nd harmonic band of Band-n257 was suppressed by over 20 dB thanks to putting the LPF in front of the antenna. The symmetricity of the directivity for beam forming was improved owing to the differential feeding.

articleTitle: Localization of Radio Sources Using Near-field DOA-Matrix Method in Distributed Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The near-field DOA-Matrix method can localize the positions of radio sources in the near field of the receiving array. This paper discusses the use of distributed arrays for enhancing the estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Vortex Beam Selection for A2G-RV Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Orbit angular momentum (OAM) based radio vortex wireless communication with the characteristic of orthogonal mode division multiplexing (MDM) enables higher spectrum efficiency (SE) than conventional multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) communications. However, MDM techniques are only suitable for line-of-sight (LOS) environments and suffer from a strict limitation in applications due to the physical property of divergence of the vortex beams. The flexibility of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) can rapidly establish LOS communication links, and the corresponding air-to-ground (A2G) channels furthest utilize the spatial distributing characteristics of the energy of vortex beams. For the A2G channel, we proposed the joint beam selection and water-filling power allocation (JBS-WPA) schemes to improve the SE of the A2G wireless communication system. Numerical results indicate that the proposed system with JBS-WPA algorithm can obtain a higher SE than conventional MDM-MIMO systems. Therefore, OAM techniques can offer a brand new solution for future air-to-ground (A2G) networks.

articleTitle: Miniaturization Design of Monopole Antenna Based on Capacitive Loading
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, three new structures of monopole antenna are proposed, which can greatly reduce the size of monopole antenna under the premise of ensuring omnidirectional radiation, high gain and high efficiency. The structures of the antenna adopt the innovative technology of capacitive loading. The performance of the proposed antennas can be obtained in three-dimensional electromagnetic field simulation. In order to understand the working mechanism of the innovative monopole antennas, the equivalent circuit model of the antennas is proposed and analyzed in this paper. The miniaturized monopole antennas can be used in short-range communication, radio communication and other equipment. The simulated and measured results of the antennas show that the innovative structures play a very significant role in miniaturizing the size of monopole, as well as in impedance matching, gain and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on UWB Tightly Coupled Array Based on AMC
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an AMC-based tightly coupled array antenna is presented, which operates in an ultra-wideband of 1.77 to 17.74 GHz (VSWR ≤ 3). Although the traditional tightly coupled array has a lower profile (less than 1/4 of the center frequency) and a wide bandwidth (more than 5:1), it is difficult to achieve a wider bandwidth because it is difficult to balance the high and low frequency radiation characteristics. When optimizing the low frequency band of the antenna, high frequency performance is affected, and vice versa. The AMC-based tightly coupled array presented in this paper, by loading a layer of frequency selective surface between the metal floors, is equivalent to high impedance to high frequency, and has little effect on the low frequency band. Compared to the traditional tightly coupled array The antenna has a wider bandwidth.

articleTitle: ToA and DoA estimation results using cylindrical array with 19GHz band in an actual outdoor environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, the use of 5th-generation mobile communication system (5G) in the millimeter wave band is assumed, and the introduction of massive MIMO in 5G is considered. Massive MIMO uses beamforming based on terminal position in an environment with a large propagation loss, such as the millimeter wave band. Therefore, it is important to understand the direction of arrival of signals in the millimeter wave band. In this report, we attempt to elucidate the relationship between power, delay time, and direction of arrival when focusing on the horizontal direction using a massive array of 192 elements in the 19 GHz band in the urban area of Niigata City. We also demonstrate the direction of arrival estimation results that were obtained using the proposed beam former (BF) method.

articleTitle: Frequency-Switchable Patch Antenna with Parasitic Ring Load for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A frequency-switchable patch antenna for millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) 5G communications is presented in this paper. The antenna is designed on a Rogers RT5880 substrate with 0.8 mm thickness, 2.2 dielectric constant, and 0.0009 loss tangent. The antenna design consists of a conventional patch antenna surrounded by a rectangular-ring parasitic load structure. By implementing and biasing an active element (diode switch) the antenna response can be switched to operate at either 22.25 GHz or 28 GHz which are two of the candidate frequency bands for the future 5G networks. Performances of the antenna in forms of single element, linear array (1×8), and planar array (4×4) have been investigated. Furthermore, the radiation performance of the planar array in the presence of the human hand is studied. The simulated results of the proposed design show good characteristics of the arrays.

articleTitle: KA Analytical Solution of Dielectric Rough Surface with Arbitrary Power Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: It is well known that Small Perturbation Method (SPM) method gives analytical expressions of electromagnetic scattering from arbitrary power spectrum rough surface. However, KA method only gives explicit analytical expressions for Gauss spectrum rough surface. This paper attempts to derive the analytical expression of KA scattering from rough surfaces with arbitrary spectrum fluctuations. It is divided into three main parts. Firstly, the paper derives the formula of traditional Kirchhoff Approximation (KA) method. Then, based on the basic spectrum, such as Gaussian Spectrum and Exponential Spectrum, the paper invents two ways Fourier Transform Method (KAF) and Convolutional Method (KAC) to solve EM scattering from complex spectrum rough surface. The numerical results show that KAC is more accurate but needs more computation and memory than KAF.

articleTitle: Effective Nonuniform Fast Fourier Transform for Calculating Sparse Array Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An effective nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) is proposed in this paper. Linear interpolation is used to calculate the virtual element excitations by exploiting periodicity in the NUFFT. The use of linear interpolation notably increases the computational efficiency for the calculation of nonuniform antenna array patterns. The computational burden and approximation errors are analyzed, and numerical results for the synthesis of a sparse antenna array through differential evolution are obtained. All results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Beam-tilt Compact Horn Antennas Loading a Half-Cylindrical Conductor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a beam-tilt compact horn antenna loading a half-cylindrical conductor for obtaining large beam tilt. The proposed antenna can tilt the radiated beam to direction of 30 degrees by using the same diameter 18mm (3λ/2) with the previously-developed antenna with 20-degree beam-tilt at 24GHz. Usefulness of the proposed antenna is verified numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Design of a Low Sidelobe Monopulse Array Antenna with Hybrid Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low sidelobe monopulse array antenna with hybrid feeding structure is proposed. The array consists of four subarrays which employ 6 × 8 microstrip patch elements on the top layer. The feed network, which is hybrid feeding structure, is composed of 1-to-48 microstrip power dividers on the top layer, microstrip to groove gap waveguide transitions and a gap waveguide-based monopulse comparator. The microstrip unequal power dividers are compact to achieve unequal amplitude distribution. And the monopulse comparator based on groove gap waveguide has low insertion loss. Hence, the array antenna achieves low sidelobe and high efficiency. The array antenna is designed with size of 400 × 320 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulated VSWR is less than 1.5 from 10.52 - 10.68 GHz, the simulated gain is 28.7 dBi at 10.6 GHz and the sidelobe level is less than -19 dB. The null depth in the difference pattern is less than -35 dB.

articleTitle: Graphene-based Dual-band Magnitude Tunable Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dynamically magnitude tunable dual-band filter using graphene loaded dual-band resonators is presented. The dual-band resonator is composed of a dual-mode centrally shorted split ring resonators and a pair of graphene flake pads. By applying biased voltage to the two sides of graphene flake pad, the transmission magnitude of two passbands can be independently tuned gradually, while the center frequencies of two passbands can still keep unchanged.

articleTitle: A Simplified Estimation Method of Propagation Loss in V2V Communication Environments considering Blocking Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In V2V (Vehicle to Vehicle) communication environments, existence of vehicles in the surrounding area influences the propagation characteristics since propagation paths suffer from blocking by the vehicles. It is therefore important to consider the effect in analysis of propagation characteristics in the environment. In this paper, we propose a simple method to calculate the propagation loss considering blocking vehicles in V2V communication environments. The method is based on the blocking ratio of the first Fresnel zone. We evaluate the accuracy of the calculation by showing the difference from those calculated using UTD (Uniform Theory of Diffraction).

articleTitle: A Wideband MMW Microstrip-line Antenna with five rings for dual circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband millimeter wave (MMW) microstrip-line antenna with five rings for dual circular polarization is proposed. The antenna is constructed by five sequentially fed microstrip-line rings, with one ring located in the center as feed line and the other four rings surrounding the center ring as a circular array. The circular polarization is realized by rings arranged in appropriate phase, which is controlled by the radii of rings. Moreover, the antenna possesses symmetric structure and two ports for dual circular polarization. Simulation results show that the antenna obtains an operating bandwidth of 12% across the 37.2～42 GHz, and the realized gain is higher than 6.7 dBic with the highest gain of 8 dBic at 38.5 GHz. Besides, the antenna is etched on one substrate and easy to fabrication.

articleTitle: Design of a 1-Bit Reconfigurable Transmitarray Element in Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An electronically reconfigurable transmitarray element designed in Ku band is presented. The proposed element using two orthogonally coupling slots structure with two PIN diodes, can be electronically controlled to generate two phase states with 180° phase difference and low transmission loss. The metal vias are added around the element to eliminate the transmission zeros under oblique incidence, and improve the transmission characteristics. In simulation, the insertion loss of two states are 1.5 dB at normal incidence. Full-wave simulation results show that the proposed element with vias loading achieves a stable performance under oblique incidences.

articleTitle: Rain Attenuation Characteristics for 21-GHz-band Satellite Broadcasting Measured by Beacon Signal
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The BSAT-4a broadcasting satellite was launched in September 2017. BSAT-4a has 12-GHz-band transponders for HDTV and UHDTV broadcasting services, as well as 21-GHz-band transponders for experiments aimed at next-generation broadcasting services. In the 21-GHz-band transponders, a beacon signal is available for observing rain attenuation and cross polarization discrimination (XPD) characteristics. We have started making measurements at a receiving earth station in Tokyo. We compared the measured rain attenuation and XPD characteristics in the 21-GHz band with the predicted characteristics specified in Rec. ITU-R P.618-13.

articleTitle: A Design of Single-Feed Quad-Beam Antenna Using Phase Shifting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A design of single-feed multi-beam antennas using phase shifting surfaces is presented in the paper. The proposed antenna is composed of a standard gain horn antenna and a transmit-array. The transmit-array are phase shifting surfaces, which could realize the function of beam convergence to make the antenna have higher gain, and achieve four beams at the same time. The unit cell of the transmit-array is composed of four metallic layers and three dielectric layers alternately arranged. The metallic layers is implemented by cascading a two-dimensional array of micro-strip square rings with circle patches inside. The transmit-array are consisted of 16 × 16 elements, and its structure is symmetrical along the X-axis and Y-axis. The whole prototype operation in X-band could generate four symmetric beams with 50° elevation separation between the beams and a peak realized gain of 11.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Control of Radiation Direction in an Aperture Array excited by a Waveguide 2-plane Hybrid Coupler
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The authors design a plate that controls the beam direction in an aperture array excited by a waveguide 2-plane hybrid coupler. The beam direction can be controlled in a range of ±18-38 deg. in the quasi H-plane, and ±27-54 deg. in the quasi E-plane at the design frequency of 66 GHz. Inductive irises are introduced into tapered waveguides in the plate and suppressed the reflection due to the narrow apertures.

articleTitle: A Frequency Selective Rasorber with Switchable Operating Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, a reconfigurable frequency selective rasorber (FSR) using dual-polarized active frequency selective surface has been proposed. The FSR is a double-layer structure. The upper layer is a resistive sheet and the bottom layer is a bandpass FSS with PIN diodes. Two layers are separated by air. The different working states of PIN diodes are able to switch operation modes of the FSR at X-band. Simulated results show a reflection band (at around 9.7GHz)/transmission band (at around 9.45GHz) between two absorption bands. The frequency with strongest reflection is different from the transparent window, a fake working frequency can be used for camouflage. The insertion loss of the transmission window is 0.32 dB. With the introduction of a transmission zero, the upper passband selectivity of the FSR gets improved.

articleTitle: Asynchronous tracking of an unknown moving interference for space radio monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study addresses the problem of geolocating an unknown moving emitter that causes uplink interference on a geostationary satellite. One common geolocation method is to utilize time difference of arrival (TDOA) of three geostationary satellites. However, when there are only two ground monitoring antennas, monitoring the downlink signals of three geostationary satellites simultaneously is not possible. To overcome this problem, we propose an asynchronous tracking method using TDOAs of three geostationary satellites and only two ground antennas.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Double Ridged Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, a miniaturized double ridged horn antenna is designed.
