Ridges with tapered width and a horn shell with tapered opening size are used to realize the miniaturization of the antenna. The overall size of the proposed antenna is only 0.442λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>×0.374λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>×0.436λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> is the wavelength at lowest operating frequency), which is significantly smaller than the traditional ones. The designed antenna achieves good performance in the range of 1.7-12.7 GHz with VSWR less than 2. The designed antenna is processed and measured. The test results are in good agreement with the simulation ones.

articleTitle: Modeling of False Scattering Center Based on Hyper-quadratic Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The scattering center theory is of great significance to radar tracking and identification of targets. For multi-component targets, the two components are coupled to produce a double scattering effect. The position of the equivalent scattering center is often not on the target surface and difficult to determine, which will cause interference to the target positioning and feature recognition. This is called a false scattering center. Taking two super quadric surface cylinder targets as an example, the calculation method of the false scattering center position generated by double scattering is given, and the scattering center model of the target is proposed. The accuracy is compared with the simulation results of the full wave method.

articleTitle: An Improved Design Method for Ring-focus Reflector Antenna with Elliptical Beam
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In order to improve the performances such as low side lobe level of the conventional ring-focus reflector antenna of variable focal distance with elliptical beam, based on the conventional design method, the aperture electrical distribution, which can enhance the design flexibility and increases the possibility to achieve desired performance, is introduced to solve the curves in long-axis plane and short-axis plane. The design example through joint optimization combining the aperture electrical distribution with the transition function which used to form sub-reflector is implemented. As a result, the side lobe level of reflector is decreased with reasonable antenna efficiency.

articleTitle: A Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna for the Millimeter Handheld Communication System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A horizontally polarized omnidirectional antenna for the millimeter handheld communication system is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of four printed dipole antennas. The operating frequency range of the antenna is from 37GHz to 39GHz. The simulation results using HFSS show that the reflection coefficient of antenna is lower than -14dB from 37GHz to 39GHz. The max gain of the antenna at 38GHz is 1.22dBi with an omnidirectional radiation pattern in E-plane. And the out-of-roundness of antenna is less than 2dB. The comparison between measured results and simulated results are also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: A Frequency-selective Rasorber Based On Thick-screen FSS
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency-selective rasorber with a transmission band between dual absorption bands based on thick-screen FSS. This rasorber consists of three layers: band-pass FSS, lower frequency absorption screen, and upper frequency absorption screen. The structure realizes a very low insertion loss in passband and stable absorption properties with wide scanning angle. It can be applied in radome technology and significantly reduce the monostatic and bistatic RCS.

articleTitle: The Spectral Characteristics of Vacuum Arc Plasma under Different Anode Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to compare the spectral characteristics of vacuum arc plasma under different anode materials. The experiment was based on the butt type contact, with diameter D=40mm and gap distance g=10mm. We used copper cathode, while the materials of anode were aluminum, iron and chromium respectively. The vacuum arc was ignited by a needle tungsten electrode, which was embedded in the cathode. A high-voltage pulse with a rise time of 8ns, and aptitude of 24kV was applied on the needle electrode. The arc current was measured by Hall sensor and the arc voltage was measured by Tektronix P6015A, respectively. The emission intensities of the inter-electrode vacuum arc plasma were collected by an optics spectrograph. The typical emission spectra of the vacuum arc plasma were obtained under copper cathode to aluminum anode, iron anode and chromium anode respectively. It can be seen that the spectra of the inter-electrode plasma concentrate in visible light band, from 300 to 700nm. The spectra mainly include different emission lines of copper, aluminum, iron, and chromium upon a lower continuum. Both the intensities and the quantity of the emission lines were increased as the current increased. Moreover the increased lines were mainly produced by the anode material.

articleTitle: A Wideband Filtering Patch Antenna Array based on Hybrid Feeding Scheme
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A wideband filtering patch antenna is implemented using a hybrid feeding scheme. The radiation element consists of a rectangular patch and two parasitic patches. A microstrip feed line loaded with two open stubs is utilized to simultaneously feed the rectangular patch through the slot and probe. With the hybrid feeding scheme, the bandwidth is increased. The bandwidth is further enhanced by the parasitic patches, which also introduce a radiation null at the upper band edge. Another radiation null at lower band edge is generated by the open stubs. Measured results show that the proposed filtering patch antenna achieves a wide 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 8.96%, achieving an average gain of 5.85 dBi within passband and out-of-band suppression levels of 9.15 dB. Based on this antenna element, a 1×4 array was also designed and fabricated to enhance the directivity.

articleTitle: Wideband Frequency Reconfigurable Metamaterial Antenna Design with Double Square SRR
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of wideband frequency reconfigurable metamaterial antenna with double square split ring resonator SRR. The design is utilizing left-handed Capacitor to enhance bandwidth. Introducing double square split ring resonator result to improvement of the matching condition. Frequency reconfiguration on the other hand is achieved by inserting PIN Diode switch in a specific slot which reconfigure wideband antenna to single band at 5.2GHz. Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Software was used to determine the effectiveness of the technique and operation of the proposed antenna. From the result obtained, the antenna has a bandwidth range of (2.4-5.4) GHz which is equivalent to fractional bandwidth of 76.92%. The antenna can be used for WLAN applications at 2.4GHz and 5.2GHz.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna Array Based on FSS Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper designed a circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna array which realizes circular polarization by loading an FSS-based polarization converter. The proposed FSS polarization converter is based on the multilayer non-resonant FSS which has a low profile. It is composed of 13 × 11 subwavelength units which the dimension is 0.18λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.18λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. The simulated results show that the axial ratio is less than 3 dB in the frequency range of 9.5 GHz to 11.3 GHz i.e. a fractional bandwidth of 17.3% within the targeted frequency band. With the FS S polarization converter loaded, there is a slightly gain reduction when compared with the original microstrip patch antenna array in the band.

articleTitle: A Leaky Waveguide with High Radiation Efficiency for Millimeter-Wave Compact-Range Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a rectangular waveguide with different width of rectangular-shaped periodic slots cutting into broad wall for generating a uniform electric field intensity wave in near-field region, is proposed and investigated. The radiation energy in near-field region of the leaky waveguide is controlled by the width of the slots. An impedance bandwidth of 12.5% for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -20 dB (from 30-34 GHz) is obtained. In addition, the radiation efficiency has reached to 80%-90% at frequency band from 30 to 34 GHz, in which the co-polarization component of electric field intensity that is 200 mm distant from the leaky waveguide fluctuates within a range of 4 dB.

articleTitle: An ENZ-Inspired Antenna with Controllable Double-Difference Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Inspired by the epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) medium, a novel planar antenna with tunable difference radiation pattern is proposed in this work, which is constructed by the series-fed two-element effective ENZ antenna array. The intriguing property of the infinite wavelength within the ENZ medium allows for the radiation independent of the antenna's geometry. In this manner, the directions as well as the gain of the four lobes can be altered flexibly via stretching the antenna elements at the same operating frequency. The fabricated prototype demonstrated a double different pattern with the measured realized gain of the four lobes higher than 4.3 dBi and the 17-dB null depth at the broadside.

articleTitle: Dual-Circularly-Polarized Dual-Beam Microstrip Patch Antenna Arrays at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, the design of array antennas for producing dual-circularly-polarized dual-beam radiation via element rotation and phasing is presented. In the pattern synthesis of an antenna array, by exploiting both radiator rotation and phased feeding for all the array elements, the beamforming for left- and right-handed circularly-polarized (LHCP and RHCP) radiated waves can be independent controlled, thus resulting in dual-circularly-polarized high-gain beams each pointing at an arbitrary direction. To verify the proposed technique, a linear array with 16-elements and a planar array containing 4×4 elements are designed and simulated. The proposed antenna arrays have a simple structure, a wide bandwidth, and high polarization purity.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Band-Switching Multiband Dual-Polarized 5G mm-Wave Antenna-in-Package (AiP) Array for Cellular Phones
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The design of a miniaturized band-switching multiband dual-polarized linear antenna-in-package (AiP) array consisting of 4 antenna elements is proposed for cellular phones with fifth generation mobile communications (5G) mm-Wave technologies. Based on |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nn</sub>| ≤ -10 dB in state #1, both the two polarizations (pol.) of the AiP array can cover from 27.21 GHz to 28.72 GHz and from 36.96 GHz to 40.17 GHz. The third generation partnership project (3GPP) bands n261 and n260 can hence be accommodated as the local main bands. The worst |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nn</sub>| values of both pol. for bands n257 in state #1 and n258 in state #2 are -6.14 dB and -6.31 dB, which both are better than -6.0 dB. Bands n257 and n258 can thus be covered as the roaming bands. The whole size of the AiP array is 0.84 mm × 4.20 mm × 19.20 mm, equivalently 0.068 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 0.34 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 1.55 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> at 24.25 GHz.

articleTitle: A simple model for outdoor to indoor penetration loss considering vertical incident angle at 5 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Recently, the next generation (5-th generation: 5G) mobile communication systems have been actively investigated all over the world. Various systems exist when considering the microwave bands after the introduction of 5G systems. Hence, the propagation characteristics when considering the interference among the systems is very important. In this paper, a simple outdoor to indoor (O2I) propagation model is proposed from the measurement at 5 GHz band. In the proposed model, we focus on the difference of the incident angle from outdoor to indoor in the vertical plane and it is shown that the proposed model realizes the additional loss by using only angles in the vertical plane.

articleTitle: A Compact CPW-fed Monopole UWB Antenna with Triple-Band Notch
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a compact triple band-notched ultrawideband (UWB) antenna fed by coplanar waveguide (CPW) is proposed. A hybrid structure of defective ring and circular patch is used to realize the radiation as well as the notch characteristic in WiMax (3.3-3.7 GHz). A cracked ring slot and an asymmetric U-shaped slot are etched on radiation patch and fed line respectively to get the second notch in WLAN (5.15-5.85 GHz) band and the third notch in satellite communication band (7.1-7.76 GHz). Except for the notch bands mentioned above, the simulated results show that the antenna achieves the 10dB impedance band from 2.52 to 12 GHz and the return loss (RL) better than -10dB. Simulated characteristics of the proposed antenna such as radiation pattern, return loss and VSWR have been presented.

articleTitle: Multi-bit All-Dielectric Reflective Metasurface for EM Wave Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-bit all-dielectric reflective metasurface is presented for EM wave manipulation. The top layer of propped metasurface consists of high index material. The unit cell is designed to act as a 1-, 2-, and 3-bit metasurface to attain better control of EM waves. For 3-bit metasurface, the eight digital states have a phase response of 0°, 45°, 90°, 135, 180°, 225°, 270°, and 315°. By using different arrangements of unit cells, the proposed metasurface is used to manipulate the EM wave. For RCS reduction application, the unit cells are arranged randomly to get a diffusion type metasurface which disperses the EM wave in all direction and hence minimizes the specular reflection. The dielectric metasurface has better efficiency than the metallic because higher Q factor is realized by using high index material.

articleTitle: Low-RCS Slot Array Antenna Using a Hybrid Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A slot array antenna with low radar cross section (RCS) is proposed by using a hybrid metasurface (HM) consisting of an anisotropic frequency selective absorber (AFSA) and a polarization rotation reflective surface (PRRS). Both the co-polarized and cross-polarized monostatic RCSs of the proposed antenna is significantly reduced for both in-band and out-of-band frequencies compared with the reference antenna. Moreover, the bistatic RCS is reduced in the angle ranges of because the incident waves are absorbed rather than reflected to other directions. The simulated results show that the RCS of the proposed slot array antenna is significantly reduced in the frequency range from 6 GHz to 18 GHz and the gain decreases about only 0.8 dB.

articleTitle: Input resistance and radiation efficiency of normal-mode helical antenna inside human body
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A normal-mode helical antenna is promising to be applied in wireless capsule endoscopy system because of its compact, cylindrical shape. To establish antenna design method, physical mechanism of antenna input resistance (R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub>) increases should be clarified. In this paper, antenna R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub> increases are clarified for changing permittivity (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>) and conductivity (σ) through electromagnetic simulation. R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub> results are shown for stomach, skin, and fat tissue for a resonant helical antenna designed at 0.2 wavelength, at MICS frequency of 402 MHz. The most noticeable increase is from fat tissue, where R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub> value increases from 0.63 Ω to 35 Ω at σ=0 [S/m] and σ=0.3 [S/m], respectively. From the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub> results, the calculation of the antenna efficiency, η<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub> was also made. Finally, the simulation results is compared to measurement results for validation.

articleTitle: Miniaturised Bandstop Frequency Selective Surface Based on Multilayer 2.5-Dimensional Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A hexagonal miniaturized frequency selective surface (FSS) based on multilayer 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) closed loop is proposed in this paper. The finite element analysis software Ansoft HFSS 19 is used to simulate the performance of FSS under different polarization modes and incident angles of electromagnetic wave. The simulation results show that the FSS resonates at 2.36 GHz and the corresponding unit size is 0.041λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.041 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. It also shows an outstanding stability under different polarization modes and incident angles.

articleTitle: Design of Transmitter for 5G Channel Emulator
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This thesis focuses on the development of millimeter wave transmitter module for wideband channel emulator application. The millimeter wave channel emulator transmitter which integrates RF front-end, IF module and baseband processing module is designed with channel bandwidth of 500MHz and output power of -80~0dBm. Due to the wide frequency band of the RF output, the RF front-end module adopts segmentation scheme, which is divided into 18-26 GHz and 26-40 GHz for mixing, amplifying and filtering. Based on the simulation and design, a prototype is developed. The test results show that the RF transmitter module has satisfactory performance and meets the design requirements.

articleTitle: Small-Size coupled-fed loop antenna for the LTE Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A small coupled loop antenna for LTE smart phones is proposed. The antenna is placed in the corner of the system plane of the smart phone, with a thickness of 6 mm, which meets the profile requirements of most mobile phones. The main part of the antenna is designed as a coupling feed ring structure. After introducing the lumped element matching circuit, the antenna can provide two wide working bands to cover LTE low band (730 - 960 MHz) and LTE middle band (1710 - 2690 MHz). In this study, the bandwidth is extended by introducing high-pass matching circuit. The simulation efficiency of the antenna is given in this paper.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Bidirectional Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A millimeter wave bidirectional dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) is presented in this paper. The proposed DRA consist two cylindrical DRs with the same size symmetrically placed on top of a squared ground plane. The two DRs are fed by a coaxial probe and excited in higher order HEM117 mode. The antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 2.60 % and an antenna gain of 5.36 dBi.

articleTitle: Flexible Rasorber Based on Graphene
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the development of radar and communication system, frequency selective rasorber (FSR) is in great need. In this paper, a flexible rasorber based on graphene is presented and investigated. A passband with small insertion loss and two absorption bands with high absorptivity below and above the passband is realized. Besides, the designed structure can be further fabricated on polyvinyl chloride (PVC) layer, which enables our rasorber to be applied in flexible situations.

articleTitle: Design of a FSS Radome with High Harmonic Emission Suppression
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A FSS radome with high harmonic emission suppression is designed in this paper. The cell structure and size of the FSS radome are determined by the better impedance matching in the operating frequency band and better suppression of the second harmonic frequency band. Under the condition of selecting the space between the FSS radome and the antenna, the impedance, the operating frequency radiation and the second harmonic radiation of the antenna with the FSS radome are simulated. The simulated results show that the FSS radome has a little influence on the impedance and the operating frequency radiation of the antenna. The FSS radome has high suppression of the second harmonic radiation of the antenna. The suppression capability is about 10dB.

articleTitle: Design of Novel Flat Bend Crossed Dipole for Wideband Phased Array Feed Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Phased Array Feed (PAF) element based on flat bend crossed dipole fed by 50-Ohm coaxial line. The PAF element is dual-polarized and made from all-metal to minimize Ohmic losses and simplify cryogenic integration. It is optimized for 4- 8 GHz band aiming to possible later integration in the SKA pathfinder PHAROS2. The proposed design can also be a good element candidate of PAF for the Five hundred meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) and Qi Tai Telescope (QTT) as well as other large radio telescopes.

articleTitle: Construction of optical needles and spot arrays using radiation pattern of collinear antenna array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An optimization-free approach is proposed for generating optical needle and bright spot arrays with controllable distributions. This is achieved by inversely focusing the radiation pattern from a collinear antenna array whose elements are placed along an optical axis and whose currents in each element also flow along the direction of that axis, situated at the focus of a 4pi configuration. The shape and central location of the nth focusing field only depend on the length l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> and the coordinate z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> of the nth element in the collinear array, respectively. The number of focal fields is determined by the number of elements in the array. The focal field is dominantly polarized along the longitudinal direction and its full width at half-maximum along the radial direction remains unchanged within the entire depth of focus. Three types of engineered focal field arrays, namely pure needle arrays, pure spot arrays, and hybrid arrays of needles and spots, are presented as examples to demonstrate the validity and flexibility of the proposed method. The light needle and bright spot arrays generated by this approach may find potential applications in multi-particle acceleration and in multi-particle trapping and manipulation.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Planar Aperiodic Sparse Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents our study on designing a planar aperiodic sparse phased array with a characteristic of the low side lobe level (SLL) at a wide beam-steered angle spanning a wide bandwidth, using the optimizing algorithm of covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES). An optimized aperiodic planar sparse array in a circular disk with a radius of 6.25λ0 has been achieved, showing the peak SLL<; -15 dB without steering the main beam and the peak SLL<; -12 dB with the main beam being steered 60° away from the broadside in a bandwidth from f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 10f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival with Coherent Sources in Time Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel method for estimating the direction of arrivals (DOA) with coherent sources in time modulated arrays (TMA) based on forward-backward smoothing (FBS) algorithm is proposed and verified. Utilizing the norm approximation method, the signals received by the array are reconstructed from enough number of sideband signals. Then the FBS and multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm are applied to obtain the DOA estimation of coherent sources. Numeric simulations are brought out to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of an element Applied in Microstrip Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel center symmetrical antenna element is proposed, whose position of feeding point is fixed even with different rotated angel. Furthermore, this element uses vertical interconnection structure to replace the RF connector in order to lower the weight and the cost, which is suitable for the appliance in microstrip reflector antenna. By commercial simulation software HFSS, the radiation pattern and axial ratio are all shown.

articleTitle: UWB-Radar Cross Section Measurements in the Fresnel Region and Real Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to approximate the specular radar cross section of a flat plate (with known dimensions) in the Fresnel region. The proposed method relies on averaging the contribution from discrete current elements at the horn antenna aperture and discrete current elements on the target. The approximations made to estimate the phase difference result in the classical flat plate radar cross section when the antennas-target distance approaches the far field. A computing time saving technique with Fresnel integrals is proposed in order to calculate the phase difference. The experimental validation of the proposed technique demonstrates reasonable agreement with the theoretical far field radar cross section.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Dual-Polarization Frequency-Selective Rasorber with Meandering Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized dual-polarization frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with meandering structure is proposed, which express a transmission window between two absorption bands. The FSR consists of a lossless layer and a lossy layer. The lossy layer is a folded cross fractal structure that four resistive sheets are loaded on unit cell. The lossless layer is a bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) consisting of two metal square rings. The methods of meandering are used to achieve miniaturization. An equivalent circuit model (ECM) is proposed to analyze operating principle of the FSR. The dimension of element is 0.126 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>*0.126 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>*0.11λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> is the wavelength corresponding to the lowest working frequency. The fractional bandwidth for reflection less than -10 dB is about 58% and a transmission window with insertion loss of -0.97 dB is obtained at 10.6 GHz. The FSR perform stable frequency response from 0 to 30 degrees for both TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-polarized Frequency Selective Surface with Reconfigurable Passband
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The letter designs a novel frequency selective surface (FSS) with reconfigurable passband. Each unit consists of upper and lower metal and the dielectric material. The upper and lower metal are the same. The upper metal consists of a folded metal ring and the cross-shaped fold line. By loading and adjusting the adjustable inductance at the four connection points of the metal ring and the cross-shaped line, the passband can be reconfigurable. When the inductance is 1nH, the passband of the FSS is 4.8-5.1GHz, moreover, the transmission coefficient is lower than -0.31dB at 4.8-5.1GHz, and lower than -9dB in the 3.3-3.6GHz. But when the inductance is 21nH, the passband of the FSS is 3.3-3.6GHz, in addition, the transmission coefficient is lower than -0.67dB at 3.3-3.6GHz, and lower than -12.3dB in the 4.8-5.1GHz. The FSS has dual-polarization since the structure has rotational symmetry.

articleTitle: Balanced-to-Unbalanced Filtering Power Divider with Stub-Loaded Dual-Mode Resonators
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a balanced-to-unbalanced filtering power divider (BTU FPD) based on stub-loaded dual-mode resonators (DMRs) with controllable bandwidth is proposed. With mixed-mode scattering matrix and even- and odd-mode theory, the closed-form analytical equations of the BTU FPD are obtained. Moreover, a pair of parallel coupling lines are acted as feedline structures to realize controllable bandwidth performance. For demonstration, the proposed BTU FPD is designed and fabricated at 1.52 GHz, and the measured results are agree well with the theoretical and simulated results.

articleTitle: MACKEY miniaturized using short-circuit plate
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Meta-surface inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY) that operates not only in a free space but also on a metal plate is proposed. In this paper, two new types of a MACKEY with a short-circuit plate are described.

articleTitle: Improvement of Isolation between Transmitting and Receiving Antennas of E-plane arranged Waveguide Slot Arrays by using Layers of Slit pairs with Half-wavelength Spacing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose loading layers of slit pairs with halfwavelength spacing over a corporate-feed waveguide slot array antenna in the 30GHz band. This structure is expected to improve the isolation between transmitting and receiving antennas arranged in the E-plane. As a result of the design, the reflection of the radiating element is suppressed under -14dB over a target band (27.8 GHz - 31.4 GHz). The isolation between two antennas using a 2x32-element model is improved by about 20 dB comparing to the conventional structure without the slit-pair layers.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-wave Circular Polarized Feed for A Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A design of a circular polarized corrugated horn feed for reflectarray antenna.The feed is composed of corrugated horn, rectangle-circle supporting structure, septum polarizer and standard waveguide converter. The simulation results show that the reflection coefficient is lower than -20 dB in the frequency range of 32 GHz-37 GHz, and the cross-polarization level of the feed antenna is lower than -30 dB at the frequency point of 35GHz.The antenna has a good symmetric radiation pattern, and the axial ratio of the antenna is lower than 1 dB in the frequency range of 32 GHz-38GHz. The antenna can be used as a feed for the reflectarray antenna.

articleTitle: A Novel Fractal UWB Antenna With Double Band-Notched Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a novel structure with a SRR ring and U-shaped slot structure on the ground is applied in the design of UWB Fractal antenna with band-notched characteristic. The double band-notched characteristic is achieved by introducing a SRR ring and U-shaped slot structure on the ground to eliminate the interference of the existed wireless local area network (WLAN) band and WIMAX band. The proposed antenna is worked on a substrate FR4 with a thickness of 1.5mm. It is studied theoretically and experimentally. The measured results show that the proposed antenna has good ultra-wideband (UWB) performances and band-notched function.

articleTitle: Non-Foster and Non-Foster-inspired Matching of Small Transmitting Antenna: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband non-Foster matching of a small transmitting antenna has been investigated for a couple of decades. However, non-Foster technology is still very challenging, due to difficulties in construction of a dedicated NIC that should assure stable operation with high-power signals. This paper discusses aforementioned basic problems and reviews two very recent approaches that imitate non-Foster matching and, at the same time, bypass stability problems. These methods employ the superposition of two coherent transmitting signals at the antenna or the incorporation of the antenna into the self-oscillating, nearly perfectly matched transmitter system. Finally, some unsolved problems and associated future research directions are highlighted.

articleTitle: A Tapered Cavity-Backed Flush-mountable Dual Mono- cone Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A tapered cavity-backed flush-mountable dual mono-cone antenna is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of three main sections: a lower mono-cone, an upper mono-cone, and an exponentially tapered cavity. In order to obtain the high frequency band operation, the upper mono-cone is located inside the lower mono-cone. The circular cavity used in the proposed antenna has a tapered wall for mitigating the deterioration of radiation performances. The proposed antenna has simulated 10-dB return loss bandwidth of 28.32 GHz ranging from 2.21 GHz to 30.44 GHz (173%) and an omni-directional radiation pattern in the operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Harmonic Suppression of Microstrip Antenna by Defected Microstrip Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a microstrip antenna with suppressed harmonics at 3.55 GHz is proposed. To achieve this operation, a short U-shaped defected microstrip structure (DMS) and a long U-shaped DMS are etched on the microstrip-feed line. The second harmonic can be reduced by using the long U-shaped DMS; meanwhile the short U-shaped DMS accomplishes the third harmonic suppression. The return loss of the proposed antenna at the fundamental, the second harmonic and the third harmonic frequencies are simulated and compared to that of the conventional microstrip antenna. It has been confirmed that the proposed antenna obtains outstanding harmonic suppression characteristic in the second- and third-harmonic frequencies.

articleTitle: A novel 3-bit coding Metasurface with Ultrathin thickness and broad band features for controlling the transmitted waves in K-band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose, a new transmission type coding metasurface with 3-bit coding resolution having the features of ultrathin thickness high efficiency and broad band of operation. Various full structures are designed based on the distribution of the designed coding particles in the 2-D spatial plane. Vortex beams generation and beam shaping functionalities are demonstrated from the designed structures with high efficiency and in broadband frequency spectrum of K-band. All the simulation results have excellent agreement with their theoretical counterparts. We are confident that the proposed ideas and designs can find potential applications in low profile transmission type optical devices.

articleTitle: Dynamic Diffusion Modeling and Scattering Characteristic of Large Number Chaff Clouds
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Firstly, the force characteristics of a single chaff in the process of dispersion and diffusion are studied, and the motion diffusion model of a single chaff is obtained. Then, the motion diffusion model of the whole chaff cloud is established by Monte Carlo method. Based on the Monte Carlo method of vector transport theory, the scattering characteristics of chaff clouds with complex shapes and inhomogeneous densities are simulated and calculated.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Gain-Reconfigurable Antennas Using A Shared Reflectarray Aperture
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a reflectarray based dual-beam gain-reconfigurable structure is proposed for dynamically controlling the gain of each beam. In this structure, two phased-array feeds are illuminating one shared reflectarray aperture. By modulating the excitation conditions for each phased-array feed and compensation phase distribution on the aperture, dual beams with different gains can be realized simultaneously, which can be useful for fully terminal coverage for the base station antennas of mobile communications. Two sets of beam states have been chosen to validate the novel structure. From the simulation results, a gain of 20.9dB is obtained for equal beam-state resulting in 39.1% aperture efficiency. For the other beam-state, two beams with 22.2dB and 18.4dB gains are achieved. The corresponding aperture efficiency are 40.4% and 31.4%, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Small Loop Antenna Operating in VLF band for Shielding Effectiveness Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a small printed loop antenna operating in the VLF band for obtaining improved AF properties. The proposed antenna is composed of a ring shape ferrite core and a printed loop antenna to reduce and simplify the antenna size. The ferrite core allows to concentrate the magnetic flux density on the ferrite surface of the antenna, which can decrease the antenna size. The results show that the antenna is suitable for accurate SE measurement of small shielded enclosures in the VLF band due to the small size and low AF level.

articleTitle: Broadband Omnidirectional Radiation Pattern Antenna With Parasitical Loops
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this communication, we present a wideband, and compact antenna with simple structure, which achieves a stable omnidirectional radiation pattern. It consists of a top loading dipole and two parasitic loops, each loop and one arm of dipole element are printed on the top and bottom sides of the dielectric substrate. A wide impedance bandwidth is obtained because using T-shaped top loading to improve the impedance at lower band. And two parasitic loops are also used to increase the bandwidth. Simulation results show that a wide impedance characteristic of about 60.9% for the reflection coefficient of less than -10 dB ranging from 1.44 to 2.70 GHz is obtained. Meanwhile, low gain variation and stable radiation patterns were achieved over the operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Sparse Near-Field Antenna Array with Multi-Focus Based on Bayesian Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An effective method for synthesizing a sparse antenna array with near-field multi-focus (NFMF) is proposed in this paper based on the Bayesian Compressive Sensing (BCS) and superposition theorem. A numerical example of three multitarget performs well and the sparsity is approximately half of the number of elements.

articleTitle: Design of a Beam Switching Circuit for Rectangular-coordinate Orthogonal 4-Multiplexing in the Non-far Region with Two-dimensional 180-degree Hybrid
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a beam switching circuit for rectangular-coordinate orthogonal multiplexing transmission system in the non-far region. In this paper, we design a 4-multiplexing waveguide beam switching circuit with uniform excitation in the 64-68 GHz band. It is composed of a 2-D hybrid and phase shifters. We design a self-compensating corrugated waveguide phase shifter and analyze the 4×4-way one-body two-dimensional beam switching hollow-waveguide circuit. The reflection is -19.4 dB at 66 GHz, and below -14.6 dB in the 64-68 GHz band. The operating frequency band of the proposed circuit is 3.0 GHz in the 64-68 GHz band. The phase error of the proposed circuit is within 15° in the 64-68 GHz band.

articleTitle: A Novel, Compact, Gain-Enhancement, Flat Lens Baesd on Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel flat lens based on metamaterials is presented in this paper. The metamaterial lens is composed of metallic lattice and squared metal patch, which can find significant gain enhancement by 3.5 dB between 1.30 GHz and 1.35 GHz without affecting the reflection coefficient of the antenna. The lens enables electromagnetic wave focus effectively and attains significant gain enhancement.

articleTitle: A Wideband and Lightweight Metamaterial Absorber by Paper-based Three-dimensional Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional ultra-wideband and lightweight metamaterial absorber is presented, which consists of vertical paper sheets with pencil-drawn resistive strip array on them backed with a metallic ground plane. It can obtain over 90% absorptivity ranging from 2.52 GHz to 40 GHz (relative bandwidth of 176.3%). We achieve the polarization-independent structure by intersecting the paper sheets to form a vertical square enclosure array structure. Each vertical paper sheet has resistive strip array on it drawn by machine controlled pencil with desired resistance. Experimental verification is carried out, which shows that the measured result is in good agreement with the simulated one. The proposed three-dimensional metamaterial absorber has advantages of lightweight, low cost, easy fabrication and eco-friendly.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Feed Open-Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A Dual-Feed Open-Slot antenna that is utilized by bottom metal frame of handset is proposed in this paper. The proposed Dual-Feed antenna has two feeding ports which are set on both sides between grounding port. Through the left feeding port, one mode is excited to cover high band(2300MHz-2700MHz). Through the right feeding port, three modes are excited to cover low band and middle band(700MHz-960MHz, 1700MHz-2200MHz). The two Feeding ports get a simulated isolation better than 12dB through filters design in matching circuits. Furthermore, through the optimal design, right feeding port can also cover 2300MHz-2400MHz. The isolation is better than 10dB and the ECC is lower than 0.07.A prototype is fabricated and measured. The isolation is better than 13dB.

articleTitle: On Study of the Method in measuring the speed and distance used for Ground Based Navigation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a method, which shouldn't be relied on the inertial navigation system (INS), to measure the speed and distance is introduced. Using the small delay in every distance measurement, the speed could be measured simultaneously; the method of signal process about the measurement is introduced; the simulation results and the analysis are given at the same time.

articleTitle: An Interference Cancellation using Antenna Selection of Inter-User for Full-Duplex MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the authors proposed a method of interference cancellation using antenna selection of inter-user for Full-duplex MIMO system. As a method of terminal-to-terminal interference cancellation, a technique by using eigen-beamforming is studied. Further interference cancellation is realized by applying the antenna selection technique to the mobile terminal when performing eigen-beamforming. The effectiveness of this method is confirmed by simulation using the ray tracing method in outdoor environment.

articleTitle: On-Body Channel Modeling Based on Different Body Heights at 28GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: With the increasing demand of high data rate, the interest of Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) working in millimeter wave (mm-wave) band is growing. This paper studies the variation of on-body propagation path loss exponent with body height at 28GHz. Specifically, the belt-to-chest link at 28 GHz has been investigated with a realistic stratified digital human body model scaled to different height. Mathematical model of the on-body path loss is proposed taking into account the effect of body height. It is concluded that the path loss exponent decreases with the increase of body height due to the influence of crawling waves on the surface of the human body.

articleTitle: Analysis of Vortex Beam Propagation Properties with the Ground Reflection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation properties of the vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) with ground are analyzed. When the vortex electromagnetic wave propagate in the real environment the reflected electromagnetic waves from the ground can affect the propagation and reception of the vortex beams. A uniform circular array (UCA) antenna is designed at 10GHz for generating the vortex beams. The corresponding electric field distribution, including the amplitude distribution and phase distribution of the vortex electromagnetic wave in some specified position is presented, and the corresponding OAM mode spectrum distribution of the vortex beam is calculated. Finally, the corresponding conclusions are summarized. These analyses could provide some references approaches for the vortex beam related studies such as in the area of radar and wireless communication.

articleTitle: Filtering Antennas Using Stacking Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Filtering antennas have been achieved more attentions for the advantages of reducing the requirement of the filter in wireless communication systems and decreasing the mutual coupling between the closely placed antennas operating at different frequencies. The most reported filtering antennas are realized by planar technology, such as cascading resonators and modifying radiator shape, which usually suffers from low gain, large planar size, or low frequency selectivity. In this paper, two filtering antennas using stacking technology with three dimensional design spaces and additional radiation nulls are proposed to solve the problem. One is the filtering antenna unit realized by stacking substrate integrated cavity (SIC)-backed slot and patch, and the other is the filtering antenna array achieved by stacking half-wavelength resonator and dipole array. The performances are given and compared.

articleTitle: A novel X-band Power Synthesizer based on SIW structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: the power requirement of wireless communication system is getting higher and higher. In order to make the output power of the system meet the design requirements, power synthesis technology is an effective way to improve the output power. In this paper, a new Y-type X-band power synthesizer based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is designed. According to the actual needs of the project, the width of the two output ports is exactly the same as the input ports. The power distribution network is connected with the right-angle bending structure, which effectively reduces the overall size of the structure. The test results show that the return loss of the new Y-type X-band power synthesizer is less than −15dB in the band of 3GHz, and its insertion loss changes between 3.6dB and 4.1dB. Broadband and Low insertion loss is the characteristics of SIW structure.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Dual-polarized Sector-loop Antenna With Compact Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarized sector-loop antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna has a sector-loop, a CPW and a microstrip-line. The antenna can realize dual-band by using resonant different modes. It is a slot basic mode in the higher band and a loop basic mode in the lower band. To realize dual-polarized performance, the antenna used a CPW to achieve vertical polarization modes and used a microstrip-line to achieve horizontal polarization modes. The simulation results show that the isolation between the two ports is better than 27dB in the dual band. The common -10dB impedance bandwidth is 310MHz (2.32-2.63GHz) and 370MHz (3.32-3.69GHz), the lower band can cover 2.4GHz WLAN and the higher band can cover 3.5GHz WiMAX. The antenna is low weight, low profile and easily assembled.

articleTitle: Development of Radio Propagation Channel Model for Millimeter-Wave Indoor Multi-Gigabit Access Links
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this article, a millimeter-wave radio channel model for indoor multi-gigabit access links was presented. In order to develop a channel model, we carried out measurement campaigns in a conference room environment. By using super-resolution path parameter estimation algorithm, multi-path rays were extracted from the measurement data, and by applying an automatic clustering algorithm to them scattering processes were identified. Then, by comparing them with ray-tracing results, it was seen that the reflected paths by side walls were well matched in both cases and they should be dominant mechanisms other than line-of-sight path. In this study, we proposed a hybrid channel model with deterministic representation by ray-tracing and stochastic representation for the surface roughness effect of reflectors based on the quasi-deterministic channel model which is adopted in IEEE 802.11ay channel model. The stochastic model parameters (intra-cluster parameters) were obtained from the clusters generated by the first-order reflected rays. The validity of the proposed model was verified via comparing the results realized by the proposed channel model with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Unit Cell of Ku/Ka Band Transmitarray for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-layer unit cell is proposed for the transmitarray (TA) application. The proposed multi-layer unit cell is composed of a H-shaped patch in the middle with three-dipoles around it. The transmitting phase of the proposed element in x- and y-polarization is controlled by two different structures. So that the unit cell can operate at Ku and Ka band independently. The unit cell achieves a phase shift range of 360° at the frequency of the 17.5GHz and 33GHz. The insertion loss at two different frequencies are lower than 2.5dB and 0.5dB, respectively. The proposed unit cell can be an effective candidate for satellite communications.

articleTitle: Design of a TDM Based FMCW Radar Imaging System with Wide FOV at 24 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper is a demonstration of combining the Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) technique with Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar for range and Angle of Arrival (AOA) estimation purposes at 24 GHz. The radar transmits the signal by a single antenna and receives the echoes by four antennas, the echo signal was sampled by the ADC and processed by the FPGA. At the end, a 24 GHz TDM based FMCW radar was fabricated and measured, the measurement result shows that the radar allows an unambiguous measurement of target range and radial velocity even in multiple target situations. In addition, the Field angle of View (FOV) is over 140°.

articleTitle: Target Direction Estimation Characteristics of Capon Algorithm in MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: MIMO radar features increasing the receiving array aperture by virtual array. This paper attempts to clarify that the estimation accuracy of Capon algorithm is higher than that of the MUSIC algorithm in MIMO radar using matched filters for transmission signal separation in receiving array.

articleTitle: Design of printed Yagi-antenna for 5G communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper takes the monopole antenna as the active element of the printed Yagi-antenna. The antenna has the advantages of small weight, small size and good directivity. The optimal matching and gain of antenna are studied. The 50 Ω microstrip feed used in the active element. Simulation results show that the average gain is 6.9dBi at 3.4 ~ 3.6 GHz, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB up to 640 MHZ bandwidth at 3.24 ~3.88GHz. The return loss reached -36dB at 3.5GHz.Through the analysis of simulation data, the requirements of 5G communication antenna are satisfied.

articleTitle: A Broadband Low-Profile Dual-Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this article, a broadband low-profile dual-polarized antenna is proposed within a height of 0.07λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength of corresponding lowest operating frequency). The proposed antenna consists of a pair of orthogonal loop dipoles, a metal ground and four parasitic patches. A prototype of the proposed antenna is constructed and test. Measured results show that the antenna achieves a S11<; -10dB from 750-870 MHz and 1.72-2.84 GHz. The isolation between the two polarization is better than 40 dB.

articleTitle: A Compact Monopole Antenna With Filtering Response for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel compact monopole antenna with filtering response for WLAN applications is presented in this paper. The antenna is composed of a capacity-loaded matching patch, two resonators, and two end-coupled monopoles. The resonators consist of wide rectangular patches and narrow shorted lines to form the resonance, and the resonators are printed on the different layers to increase the design flexibility. Two meandering monopoles are located at the edges of the top layer with capacitive coupling at each other's end. The mutual couplings between the meander monopoles are utilized to produce two radiation nulls at the two band-edges. Based on the design method, the prototype of the proposed antenna was designed, fabricated and measured. The measured results show that the antenna has a broad bandwidth of 16% for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><; -10 dB. Also, ideal omnidirectional radiation patterns, and steep band-edge selectivity with two radiation nulls are achieved for the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Multi-band Microstrip to Co-planar Stripline transitions based on electromagnetic coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Novel designs of planar Microstrip (MS) to coplanar stripline (CPS) transitions are presented in this paper. These transitions convert unbalanced transmission line Microstrip to a balanced transmission line coplanar stripline using an exponential taper. Measured insertion loss of one of the transition is less than 0.85 dB and return loss is better than 10 dB in the frequency bands around 1.7GHz, 5.1GHz and 8.5GHz. Design guidelines are provided and structure of this transition can be slightly adjusted to meet the desired output impedance and bandwidth. Transition designs are validated by back-to-back balanced and unbalanced configurations and measured using Vector Network analyzer. Measurement results agree well with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: An Efficient Synthesizing Method for Sparse Linear Scanning Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article introduces a novel sparse array synthesis method that provides a possibility to quickly obtain a scanning array with low sidelobe performance. The combination of traditional genetic algorithms and machine learning algorithms greatly reduces the amount of computational time and resources. Both inter element spacing and input amplitude distribution are optimized, and a sparse linear array having 24 elements is synthesized with an aperture of 15.5 wavelength. Compared to traditional genetic algorithms, this method can greatly reduce the synthesis time.

articleTitle: Integrated Architecture of Active Phased Array Antennas for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The applications and prospects of millimeter wave technology for radar detections and communications are introduced firstly in this paper. The corresponding critical technologies are analyzed subsequently. Due to the difference between these applications and technologies characteristics, the design routes of millimeter wave active phased array antennas and corresponding integrated architectures are studied and then proposed, main technologies focuses in these solutions, such as architecture, antenna elements, microwave devices and package integration are also suggested.

articleTitle: Design a Scaled Model of Platform-Mounted HF Antenna Using the Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Many high-frequency (HF) antennas have significantly smaller dimensions than the wavelength at which they operate and thus suffer from narrow bandwidths. This paper examines how a platform mounted antenna can be used to excite the characteristic modes (CMs) of the platform itself to increase the overall bandwidth of the system. We use the theory of CMs to identify the appropriate platform modes and determine the practical means of exciting them. We propose a scaled model at a higher frequency of 860 MHz so that experiment results can be easily achieved.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Dual-band Semicircular Half-mode Patch Antenna for Water Utility AMI Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized dual-band half-mode patch antenna for water utility Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a semicircular patch with a shorting via to generate the higher order mode. In order to reduce the size in half, the proposed antenna adopts a half-mode concept. The radius of the proposed antenna is 209 mm and the height is 30 mm. The simulated 10-dB return loss bandwidths are 3 MHz (264 MHz - 267 MHz) at the low band and 10 MHz (907 MHz - 917 MHz) at the high band. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has an omni-directional radiation pattern with a maximum gain of 2.4 dBi at the low band and a directional radiation pattern with a maximum gain of 7.7 dBi at the high band.

articleTitle: Application of Inhomogeneous-Patterned EM Metasurfaces in Microwave Power Collection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) metasurfaces have found many applications in perfect absorbers. Inhomogeneous-patterned EM metasurfaces not only ensure high beam collection efficiency, but also favor rectifying efficiency in microwave power collection. Theory of power collecting metasurface is discussed and applications of inhomogeneous-patterned MPC metasurfaces are discussed.

articleTitle: Graphene Film Based CPW-fed Antenna for Wearable Application
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a CPW-fed antenna based on graphene film for wearable applications The conductivity of graphene film is 1.1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> S/m. The new antenna with flexible substrate has the advantages of excellent flexibility, smaller size and lighter weight, which is suitable for human wear. The proposed antenna covers the frequency range from 4.22 GHz to 10.36 GHz for a |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| greater than -10 dB.

articleTitle: Utilization of the V2X Radio Channels Temporal Stationarity for Communication and Radar Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the possibilities of utilizing the stationarity of the vehicle to everything (V2X) radio channel for applications in the field of communication as well as passive radar. The stationarity can be interpreted as a measure of how severely the radio channel changes. We compute it in the temporal domain using the generalized local scattering function (GLSF) and its collinearity. Knowing about the stationarity can enable us to adapt communication and passive radar systems to make them more efficient and reliable at the same time.

articleTitle: Metasurface with Phase and Amplitude Modulations
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Benefiting from the capability of providing a certain phase gradient on the interface between two media, metasurfaces have shown great promise for controlling the outgoing electromagnetic (EM) waves arbitrarily. In some applications, both phase and amplitude profiles are required simultaneously. Here, we propose a new type of metasurface with both phase and amplitude modulations, which is composed of C-shaped particles. The designed metasurface can shape reflected beams flexibly. Meanwhile, the intensities of the reflected beams can be modulated independently using both amplitude and phase responses.

articleTitle: Estimation of protection distance for RF field strength in quasi-far field around microwave WPT apparatus
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we measured electromagnetic field strength characteristics near the microwave WPT apparatus in the quasi-far field distance (in several meters) and investigated the method of estimating the protection distance from the station by calculating the electromagnetic field strength. For the measurement method and the protection distance calculation the investigation was made with reference to IEC 62232, and ITU-T K.52, K.61 which prescribes the safety protection evaluation method for installing the radio base stations of telecommunications carriers. As a result for this model with rectangular microstrip antenna, it was found that if the transmission power is 30 W or less at 915MHz, the protection distance is estimated within 0.5 m under the reference level satisfied.

articleTitle: Predicting Outdoor Angular Characteristics and Power Distribution of Wireless LAN Signal Leaking from an Office Building
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper we predict angular characteristics of indoor-to-outdoor radio wave propagation and a probability density function of signal power leaking from an office building at 2442 MHz and 5200 MHz for a wireless LAN access point by using a large-scale electromagnetic field simulation based on the FDTD method. A numerical model of office building taking detail the floor plan and layouts into account is prepared for calculations. We evaluate the received signal strength indication on an outdoor observation surface which is spaced apart from the access point by a constant distance. The signal power distribution composes of several parts depending upon the azimuth angles measured from the wireless LAN access point. Each of them can be modelled by a Gaussian distribution if the path loss exponents are assumed to be constant in each angular region. Hence, the probability density function of signal leaking from the office building can be accurately predicted with a Gaussian mixture distribution.

articleTitle: Two Shared-Aperture Antennas as a Building Block for Four-Port MIMO Array
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a four-antenna MIMO array composed of two shared-aperture building blocks is provided. The proposed building block is composed of a loop antenna and a slot antenna, in which the loop antenna and the slot antenna share the same rectangular clearance. Without any external decoupling structure, the proposed four-antenna MIMO array yields desirable isolation of better than 16.5 dB across the desired bands (3.4-3.6 GHz). And the ECC (envelope correlation coefficients) is much better than 0.1. Consequently, the proposed MIMO array is a good candidate for future metal-rimmed smartphone.

articleTitle: Side Lobe Suppression of Marine-Radar Linear Array Antenna by a Reflectionless Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a side lobe suppression technique of a marine radar linear slot array antenna by a reflectionless metasurface. The metasurface introduces position-dependent phase shifts so that the phase across the entire aperture can be uniform. It is numerically shown that the metasurface drastically suppresses the maximum side lobe level at 9.41 GHz to be below -24 dB in both the E and H planes, and as a consequence, the peak gain of the main lobe is increased by 1.4 dB.

articleTitle: Wideband Linear to Circular Transmissive type THz Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed a wideband transmissive type linear to circular polarization converter from 1.02 THz to 1.48 THz based on metasurfaces. The proposed unit cell is bi-layered with a dielectric spacer sandwiched in between metasurfaces. Simulation results show that the proposed structure is able to convert linear polarization to circular polarization and behaves equally well with both horizontal and vertical incident polarization in wide range of frequencies from 1.02 THz to 1.48 THz. Compared to previous designs the proposed structure has wider bandwidth of operation..

articleTitle: Possible Liquid Candidates for Liquid Microwave Components
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The selection of proper liquid is critical for liquid microwave components. In this paper, possible liquid candidates are presented. 3 types of liquids, namely water-based liquids, organic liquids and the transformer oil with 9 liquid samples were measured and compared. The electrical properties and their potential applications are investigated. These results could be a valuable reference for liquid microwave component designs.

articleTitle: Influence of Maritime Tropospheric Duct on Ocean-Scattered Low-Elevation GPS Signal Propagation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a detailed analysis of the ocean-scattered low-elevation global positioning system (GPS) signal propagation in tropospheric duct is made using the conventional random rough surface scattering model and the parabolic equation (PE) method. In order to explore the influence of duct structures on ocean-scattered GPS signals, a suite of simulations are conducted in normal atmosphere, evaporation duct, surface duct with and without a base layer, and range-dependent duct profiles. From the simulated results, surface duct without a base layer and the horizontal variation of the duct profiles can affect the GPS ocean-scattered signal propagation seriously.

articleTitle: EBG-based Dielectric Image Guide For 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures are studied and used in the design of a broadband transmission medium for 5G applications. Combined with the dielectric image guide, mushroom-like EBG units are aligned along the guiding channel to suppress side leakages and avoid the coupling effect from other integrated components. At the same time, a tapered CPW to SIW transition structure is used as the mode launcher to achieve a broadband and smooth mode conversion. Simulation results show that this new proposed waveguide efficiently works in the targeted frequency range.

articleTitle: Frequency Scanning Planar Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency scanning planar lens antenna operating from 9GHz to 11GHz. A four layered frequency selective surface (FSS), consisting of 9×9 cells, is designed as the lens for phase compensation. Based on Fermat's principle and transmission characteristics of the FSS, frequency scanning performances could be realized. A quasi-Yagi antenna is selected and embedded as the source at focal point to radiate well in the required band. The simulated S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> below -10dB is from 7.7GHz to 13GHz, which covers the required band. It is demonstrated that the scan angle is from -34° to -26° with over 10dBi gain, as frequency rises from 9GHz to 10GHz. The results in simulation validate the frequency scanning performances of the planar lens antenna well.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Dual-band Antenna Loaded with Left-handed Metamaterial for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact printed antenna working for WLAN and WiMAX applications is presented, which is composed of a T-shaped monopole and two novel symmetrical left-handed metamaterial (LHM) unit cells. The T-shaped monopole with a partial defected ground plane is designed for the middle WiMAX band as a feed antenna. The LHM unit cells is excited by the feed antenna, which generate a passband of the lower WLAN band and improve the performance of gains and radiation patterns simultaneously. The load of LHM unit cells makes the antenna realize a miniaturized size of 0.25 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.13 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.01 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength of 3.5 GHz. The simulation results present the impedance bandwidths are 40 and 360 MHz for the 2.5 and 3.5 GHz bands, respectively, and the radiation patterns are approximately omnidirectional in H-plane.

articleTitle: Study on Scattering Characteristics of Cylindrical Non-Uniform Plasma
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper based on multilayer cylinder theory of electromagnetic wave scattering [1],[7]. The scattering properties of cylindrical non-uniform plasma in GHz band are calculated and analyzed. The results show: by using various Bessel function ratios and Bessel function logarithmic derivatives to calculate cylindrical non-uniform plasma, a more stable solution can be obtained.

articleTitle: Tunable SIW Slot Antenna Constructed by High Permittivity Material
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) bowtie slot antenna with tunable operation frequency is presented. The tunable is done by covering a high permittivity BST dielectric thick film into the radiation slot similar to a bowtie. The radiation frequency is sensitive to the variation of the dielectric constant of the Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) ceramic. Specifically, the return loss up to -36dB is observed at the center frequency of 6.07GHz when the dielectric constant of BST is 330. The center frequency shifts from 5.31GHz-7.17GHz when the dielectric constant of the BST increases from 490 to 180. Within the tunable frequency range, the antenna gains are more than 5dBi. The radiation patterns and the gains are almost not affected by the variation of the dielectric constant of BST, which shows outstanding features of this very compact and easy fabricated tunable antenna. As a result, the presented antenna has great potential for the applications in tunable frequency selection metamaterials devices.

articleTitle: Wideband OAM generator based on high order meta-frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low profile wideband transmitarray for generating focusing orbital angular momentum (OAM) wave based on high order meta-frequency selective surface is proposed in this paper. The employed meta-FSS element with a fourth-order band-pass filter property, which exhibits the merit if low profile, high transmissivity and wide angular stability. A panel consisting of 17×17 elements is designed to generate +1 mode OAM wave at broadside direction. Simulated results show that the proposed structure can convert the incident spherical phase front into OAM beam helical phase distribution from 11.0 GHz to 13.0 GHz.

articleTitle: Planar Metasurface Lens based on Pancharatnum -Berry phase mechanism for efficient focusing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a novel subwavelength scatterer based on half wave plate principle, i.e., π phase retardation between two orthogonal polarizations. The scatterer has very small thickness around λ/20 and is capable to provide high transmission of cross-polarized circular polarized wave. The full phase control in the range of 0-2π is achieved by rotating the scatterer based on Pancharatnum-Berry Phase principle. The proposed scatterer is then utilized to demonstrate planar lens that could focus energy at the desired spot.

articleTitle: A Unified Approach for Treatment of Frequency-Dependent Materials in FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a unified and efficient approach for treatment of frequency-dependent materials in the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method by performing fast inverse Laplace transform to find the time-domain impulse response of frequency-dependent quantities such as electric and magnetic susceptibility. Then, Prony's method is applied to extract parameters to be directly incorporate into the FDTD formulation. Examples of applying the proposed method to dielectric and magnetic materials are demonstrated and numerically validated.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Multi-particle Mixed Haze Condensed Particles
publicationTitle: 2019 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Atmospheric aerosol is an important part of the earth-atmosphere system. Climate and environmental effects caused by aerosol have attracted wide attention. The scattering characteristics of aerosol particles, such as scattering, absorption, extinction efficiency factor, asymmetry factor and single albedo, are important parameters for assessing atmospheric environmental pollution, studying climate radiation and atmospheric light transmission. In this paper, a model of multi-component aerosol mixed agglomerated particle system is constructed.
